    from scripts.preprocessing.pupil_processing import process_pupil

    out = {"pupil": None, "eda": None, "hrv": None, "scr_onsets": None, "dilations": None}
    try:
        pup = process_pupil(pid)["pupil_mean_bc"].dropna()
        out["pupil"] = pup if len(pup) else None
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        eda = process_eda(pid)
        ph = eda["eda_phasic"].dropna()
        out["eda"] = ph if len(ph) else None
        peaks = np.flatnonzero(np.nan_to_num(eda["scr_peaks"].to_numpy()) > 0)
        if len(peaks) and len(ph):
            out["scr_onsets"] = _onsets_from_peaks(eda["eda_phasic"].to_numpy(),
                                                   eda.index, peaks)
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        nn = process_hrv(pid)[0]
        if nn is not None and len(nn.dropna()):
            nn = nn.dropna()
            out["hrv"] = pd.Series(60000.0 / nn.to_numpy(), index=nn.index)  # ms to beats/min
    except Exception:
        pass
    if out["pupil"] is not None:
        out["dilations"] = _dilation_times(out["pupil"])
    return out


def _onsets_from_peaks(phasic, index, peak_pos):
    """A response is recorded at its peak, but the claim is about when it begins, so each
    onset is the local minimum of the phasic component in the six seconds before its peak."""
    fs = max(1.0, len(index) / max(1e-9, (index[-1] - index[0]).total_seconds()))
    back = int(round(6 * fs))
    out = []
    for p in peak_pos:
        lo = max(0, p - back)
        seg = phasic[lo:p + 1]
        if not len(seg) or not np.isfinite(seg).any():
            continue
        out.append(index[lo + int(np.nanargmin(seg))])
    return pd.DatetimeIndex(sorted(set(out))) if out else None


def _dilation_times(pupil):
    """Peaks in the baseline-corrected diameter, taken as dilation events."""
    v = pupil.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    if len(v) < 5:
        return None
    pk, _ = find_peaks(v, prominence=DILATION_PROMINENCE_MM)
    return pupil.index[pk] if len(pk) else None


def to_grid(series, t0, n):
    """One signal on the shared grid, linearly interpolated, NaN outside its own span."""
    g = np.full(n, np.nan)
    if series is None or len(series) < 2:
        return g
    t = (series.index.view("int64") / 1e9) - t0
    v = series.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    ok = np.isfinite(v)
    if ok.sum() < 2:
        return g
    t, v = t[ok], v[ok]
    grid = np.arange(n) / GRID_HZ
    inside = (grid >= t[0]) & (grid <= t[-1])
    g[inside] = np.interp(grid[inside], t, v)
    return g


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- columns


def _zwin(x, w):
    """Every trailing window of length w, standardised within itself. Rows whose window
    holds a missing sample, or no variation, are left as NaN."""
    win = sliding_window_view(x, w)
    m = win.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    sd = win.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    z = (win - m) / np.where(sd < 1e-12, np.nan, sd)
    return z


def pair_columns(a, b, w, max_lag):
    """The plain correlation and the strongest correlation over shifts, for every window
    ending at each grid point. Returned aligned to the end of the window."""
    n = len(a)
    za, zb = _zwin(a, w), _zwin(b, w)
    plain = np.nanmean(za * zb, axis=1)
    plain[~np.isfinite(za).all(axis=1) | ~np.isfinite(zb).all(axis=1)] = np.nan

    best = np.full(len(plain), np.nan)
    for lag in range(-max_lag, max_lag + 1):
        if lag == 0:
            cand = plain
        else:
            # b shifted by lag: compare window i of a with window i+lag of b
            src = np.arange(len(plain)) + lag
            ok = (src >= 0) & (src < len(plain))
            cand = np.full(len(plain), np.nan)
            zb_sh = zb[src[ok]]
            cand[ok] = np.nanmean(za[ok] * zb_sh, axis=1)
        take = np.isfinite(cand) & (~np.isfinite(best) | (np.abs(cand) > np.abs(best)))
        best[take] = cand[take]

    pad = np.full(w - 1, np.nan)
    return np.concatenate([pad, plain]), np.concatenate([pad, best])


def event_columns(dilations, onsets, t0, n, w):
    """Responses beginning within three seconds after a dilation, counted in each window."""
    cnt = np.zeros(n)
    if dilations is None or onsets is None or not len(dilations) or not len(onsets):
        return np.full(n, np.nan), np.full(n, np.nan)
    d = np.sort((dilations.view("int64") / 1e9) - t0)
    o = np.sort((onsets.view("int64") / 1e9) - t0)
    # a response counts once, against the most recent dilation at most three seconds before
    j = np.searchsorted(d, o, side="right") - 1
    keep = (j >= 0) & (o - d[np.clip(j, 0, None)] <= EVENT_AFTER_S) & (o - d[np.clip(j, 0, None)] >= 0)
    hits = o[keep]
    idx = np.clip((hits * GRID_HZ).astype(int), 0, n - 1)
    np.add.at(cnt, idx, 1)
    run = np.convolve(cnt, np.ones(w), mode="full")[:n]
    return run, run / (w / GRID_HZ)


def block_for(pid, sig, idx_utc, w_s, rotate=None):
    """The eight columns for one visitor at one window length, read off at each label
    second. `rotate` rotates one signal of each pair, giving the surrogate."""
    w = int(round(w_s * GRID_HZ))
    max_lag = int(round(MAX_LAG_S * GRID_HZ))
    t = idx_utc.view("int64") / 1e9
    t0 = t[0] - w_s - 1
    n = int(np.ceil((t[-1] - t0) * GRID_HZ)) + 1
    if n < w + max_lag + 2:
        return pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx_utc, columns=COLS)

    g = {k: to_grid(sig[k], t0, n) for k in ("pupil", "eda", "hrv")}
    if rotate is not None:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(rotate)
        # rotating keeps each signal's own rhythm and distribution and breaks only the
        # timing between the two; the shift is never near zero or a whole period
        for k in ("eda", "hrv"):
            s = rng.integers(int(5 * GRID_HZ), max(int(5 * GRID_HZ) + 1, n - int(5 * GRID_HZ)))
            g[k] = np.roll(g[k], int(s))

    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=np.arange(n), columns=COLS, dtype=float)
    for a, b, tag in PAIRS:
        plain, best = pair_columns(g[a], g[b], w, max_lag)
        out[f"r_{tag}"] = plain
        out[f"rl_{tag}"] = best
    cnt, rate = event_columns(sig["dilations"], sig["scr_onsets"], t0, n, w)
    out["scr_after_n"], out["scr_after_rate"] = cnt, rate

    take = np.clip(((t - t0) * GRID_HZ).astype(int), 0, n - 1)
    res = out.iloc[take].copy()
    res.index = idx_utc
    return res


def load_all(df, n_jobs=-1):
    """Every visitor's signals, read once. The raw preprocessing is the expensive part and
    the surrogate repeats the block twenty times, so it must not be repeated with it."""
    pids = sorted(df.participant.unique())
    sigs = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs)(delayed(load_signals)(p) for p in pids)
    return dict(zip(pids, sigs))


def build(df, w_s, sigs, rotate=None):
    """The block for every row of one stream."""
    frames = []
    for pid, sig in sigs.items():
        sub = df[df.participant == pid]
        idx = pd.DatetimeIndex(sub["utc"])
        b = block_for(pid, sig, idx, w_s, rotate)
        b.index = sub.index
        frames.append(b)
    return pd.concat(frames).reindex(df.index)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scoring


def score(X, y, groups):
    splits = list(LeaveOneGroupOut().split(X, y, groups=groups))
    res = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(delayed(_fold_predict)(standard_model(), X, y, groups, tr, te)
                              for tr, te in splits)
    return _summarize(res)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--surrogates", type=int, default=SURROGATES)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    streams = ("rcea",) if args.smoke else ("rcea", "retro")
    windows = (WINDOWS_S[0],) if args.smoke else WINDOWS_S
    nsur = 2 if args.smoke else args.surrogates

    rows = []
    for stream in streams:
        df, base = load(stream)
        if args.smoke:
            keep = sorted(df.participant.unique())[:4]
            df = df[df.participant.isin(keep)].reset_index(drop=True)
        print(f"\n{stream}: {len(df):,} rows, {df.participant.nunique()} visitors", flush=True)

        sigs = load_all(df)
        usable = sum(1 for v in sigs.values() if v["pupil"] is not None or v["eda"] is not None)
        print(f"  signals read for {usable} of {len(sigs)} visitors", flush=True)

        for w_s in windows:
            blk = build(df, w_s, sigs)
            got = int(blk.notna().any(axis=1).sum())
            print(f"  window {w_s:>2}s: {got:,} of {len(df):,} rows carry a value", flush=True)
            for axis in ("valence", "arousal"):
                y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
                ok = np.isfinite(y)
                s = score(blk[ok], y[ok], df["participant"][ok])
                rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, window_s=w_s, arm="observed",
                                 ccc_mean=s["mean_CCC"], ccc_sd=s["std_CCC"], folds=s["n_folds"]))
                print(f"    {axis:8s} observed  CCC {s['mean_CCC']:+.4f}", flush=True)

            sur = []
            for r in range(nsur):
                sblk = build(df, w_s, sigs, rotate=RANDOM_SEED + r)
                for axis in ("valence", "arousal"):
                    y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
                    ok = np.isfinite(y)
                    ss = score(sblk[ok], y[ok], df["participant"][ok])
                    sur.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, window_s=w_s,
                                    arm=f"surrogate{r}", ccc_mean=ss["mean_CCC"],
                                    ccc_sd=ss["std_CCC"], folds=ss["n_folds"]))
                print(f"    surrogate {r + 1}/{nsur} done", flush=True)
            rows += sur
            pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "crosssensor_partial.csv", index=False)

    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "crosssensor.csv", index=False)
    print(f"\nwritten to {OUT_DIR / 'crosssensor.csv'}")

    obs = out[out.arm == "observed"]
    sur = out[out.arm != "observed"]
    summary = {}
    for (st, ax, w), g in obs.groupby(["stream", "axis", "window_s"]):
        s = sur[(sur.stream == st) & (sur.axis == ax) & (sur.window_s == w)]["ccc_mean"]
        summary[f"{st}/{ax}/{w}s"] = {
            "observed": round(float(g.ccc_mean.iloc[0]), 4),
            "surrogate_mean": round(float(s.mean()), 4) if len(s) else None,
            "surrogate_p95": round(float(s.quantile(0.95)), 4) if len(s) else None,
            "beats_surrogate": bool(len(s) and g.ccc_mean.iloc[0] > s.quantile(0.95))}
    (OUT_DIR / "crosssensor_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=1))
    for k, v in summary.items():
        print(f"  {k:22s} observed {v['observed']:+.4f}  surrogate p95 "
              f"{v['surrogate_p95']}  beats: {v['beats_surrogate']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/exp2_fusion.py.text:
"""Experiment 2, step three: the combination mechanisms, over every sensor subset.

Five sensors give 31 non-empty subsets: 5 single sensors, 10 pairs, 10 triples, 5 quadruples
and the full set. Each is run under three mechanisms, so the table can be read down the
subsets or across the mechanisms:

  early        all the subset's features concatenated into one model
  late_simple  one model per sensor, predictions averaged with equal weight
  late_ccc     the same, weighted by each sensor's own score

The full set is also run with the eight cross-sensor columns added to the early-fusion
matrix, which is the arm that isolates what the block of Section 3.4.2 contributes.

Every arm is scored on the same rows: every second with a valid annotation for the slice,
not the smaller set where all five sensors happen to be usable at once. A sensor's features
are imputed inside the fold like any other, so a sensor produces a prediction for every row
and the subsets stay comparable.

The late-fusion weights are computed per fold from the training participants alone. Taking
each sensor's overall Experiment 1 score would let the held-out visitor's own rows set the
weight it is scored under.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_fusion --smoke    # a few subsets, one stream
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_fusion --late     # late fusion only, minutes
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_fusion            # everything

A caution recorded here because the table invites it: with 31 subsets and a selection
resolution of 0.08, the best subset is not evidence that that subset is better. The table
is reported as a description of how the mechanisms and the subset sizes behave, and no
subset is selected from it.
"""
import argparse
import itertools
import json
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from sklearn.model_selection import LeaveOneGroupOut

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from scripts.alignment_comparison.alignment_ccc import _fold_predict, _summarize
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_alignment import cols_for, load, standard_model
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_crosssensor import build as build_block, load_all as load_sigs
from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT
from scripts.modeling.ccc_metrics import concordance_correlation_coefficient as ccc

SENSORS = ("pupil", "eda", "hrv", "speech_acoustics", "speech_content")
SHORT = {"pupil": "P", "eda": "E", "hrv": "H", "speech_acoustics": "Sa", "speech_content": "Sc"}
AXES = ("valence", "arousal")
OUT_DIR = OUT / "exp2"


def subsets():
    """Every non-empty subset, smallest first, so the table reads by size."""
    out = []
    for k in range(1, len(SENSORS) + 1):
        out += [tuple(c) for c in itertools.combinations(SENSORS, k)]
    return out


def oof_per_sensor(df, base, axis):
    """One model per sensor per fold, on the shared row universe. Returns a frame of
    out-of-fold predictions, one column per sensor, aligned to df's rows."""
    y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
    groups = df["participant"]
    pred = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=df.index, columns=list(SENSORS))
    for s in SENSORS:
        cols = [c for c in cols_for(df, s) if c in base]
        if not cols:
            continue
        X = df[cols]
        res = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(
            delayed(_fold_predict)(standard_model(), X, y, groups, tr, te)
            for tr, te in LeaveOneGroupOut().split(X, y, groups=groups))
        for _, row_index, _, yhat in res:
            pred.loc[row_index, s] = yhat
    return pred


def per_participant_ccc(y, yhat, groups, keep=None):
    """Mean, spread and fold count. `keep`, when given, collects the per-participant values
    the mean is taken over, so the appendix can report the range as well as the centre."""
    vals = []
    for p in groups.unique():
        m = (groups == p).to_numpy()
        if m.sum() < 5 or not np.isfinite(yhat[m]).any():
            continue
        ok = np.isfinite(yhat[m])
        if ok.sum() < 5:
            continue
        v = float(ccc(y[m][ok], yhat[m][ok]))
        vals.append(v)
        if keep is not None:
            keep.append((p, v))
    return (float(np.mean(vals)), float(np.std(vals)), len(vals)) if vals else (np.nan, np.nan, 0)


def late_fuse(pred, y, groups, subset, weighted):
    """Average the subset's predictions for each row. Weights, when used, come from the
    training participants of that fold only, and a sensor scoring below zero is floored so
    that a negative weight cannot invert its prediction."""
    out = np.full(len(y), np.nan)
    P = pred[list(subset)].to_numpy(float)
    for p in groups.unique():
        te = (groups == p).to_numpy()
        if not te.any():
            continue
        if weighted:
            w = []
            for j, s in enumerate(subset):
                tr = ~te & np.isfinite(P[:, j])
                w.append(max(0.0, ccc(y[tr], P[tr, j])) if tr.sum() > 5 else 0.0)
            w = np.asarray(w, float)
            if w.sum() <= 0:
                w = np.ones(len(subset))
        else:
            w = np.ones(len(subset))
        blk = P[te]
        avail = np.isfinite(blk)
        wr = np.where(avail, w[None, :], 0.0)
        tot = wr.sum(axis=1)
        num = (np.where(avail, blk, 0.0) * wr).sum(axis=1)
        out[te] = np.where(tot > 0, num / np.where(tot == 0, 1, tot), np.nan)
    return out


def early_score(df, base, subset, axis, extra=None):
    cols = [c for s in subset for c in cols_for(df, s) if c in base]
    if not cols:
        return dict(mean_CCC=np.nan, std_CCC=np.nan, n_folds=0)
    X = df[cols]
    if extra is not None:
        X = pd.concat([X, extra], axis=1)
    y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
    groups = df["participant"]
    res = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(
        delayed(_fold_predict)(standard_model(), X, y, groups, tr, te)
        for tr, te in LeaveOneGroupOut().split(X, y, groups=groups))
    return _summarize(res)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--late", action="store_true", help="late fusion only")
    ap.add_argument("--block-window", type=int, default=5,
                    help="the cross-sensor window Section 3.4.2 carries forward")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    streams = ("rcea",) if args.smoke else ("rcea", "retro")
    subs = subsets()
    if args.smoke:
        subs = [s for s in subs if len(s) in (1, 2, 5)][:6]

    rows, folds = [], []
    for stream in streams:
        df, base = load(stream)
        if args.smoke:
            keep = sorted(df.participant.unique())[:6]
            df = df[df.participant.isin(keep)].reset_index(drop=True)
        print(f"\n{stream}: {len(df):,} rows, {df.participant.nunique()} visitors", flush=True)

        block = None
        if not args.late:
            block = build_block(df, args.block_window, load_sigs(df))
            print(f"  cross-sensor block at {args.block_window}s built", flush=True)

        for axis in AXES:
            y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
            groups = df["participant"]
            pred = oof_per_sensor(df, base, axis)
            print(f"  {axis}: per-sensor predictions done", flush=True)

            for sub in subs:
                tag = "+".join(SHORT[s] for s in sub)
                for weighted, name in ((False, "late_simple"), (True, "late_ccc")):
                    if len(sub) == 1 and weighted:
                        continue  # one sensor cannot be weighted against anything
                    yh = late_fuse(pred, y, groups, sub, weighted)
                    keep = []
                    m, sd, nf = per_participant_ccc(y, yh, groups, keep)
                    folds += [dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, subset=tag, mechanism=name,
                                   participant=pp, ccc=vv) for pp, vv in keep]
                    rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, subset=tag, size=len(sub),
                                     mechanism=name, ccc_mean=m, ccc_sd=sd, folds=nf))
                if not args.late:
                    s = early_score(df, base, sub, axis)
                    rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, subset=tag, size=len(sub),
                                     mechanism="early", ccc_mean=s["mean_CCC"],
                                     ccc_sd=s["std_CCC"], folds=s["n_folds"]))
                    oofp = s.get("oof_predictions")
                    if oofp is not None and len(oofp):
                        for pp, g in oofp.groupby("participant"):
                            folds.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, subset=tag,
                                              mechanism="early", participant=pp,
                                              ccc=float(ccc(g.y_true.to_numpy(),
                                                            g.y_pred.to_numpy()))))
                    if len(sub) == len(SENSORS) and block is not None:
                        s2 = early_score(df, base, sub, axis, extra=block)
                        rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, subset=tag + "+block",
                                         size=len(sub), mechanism="early_plus_block",
                                         ccc_mean=s2["mean_CCC"], ccc_sd=s2["std_CCC"],
                                         folds=s2["n_folds"]))
                print(f"    {tag:16s} done", flush=True)
            pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "fusion_partial.csv", index=False)

    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "fusion.csv", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(folds).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "fusion_perfold.csv", index=False)
    print(f"\nwritten to {OUT_DIR / 'fusion.csv'} and fusion_perfold.csv "
          f"({len(folds):,} per-participant scores)")

    piv = out.groupby(["size", "mechanism"]).ccc_mean.mean().unstack().round(4)
    print("\nmean CCC by subset size and mechanism:")
    print(piv.to_string())
    (OUT_DIR / "fusion_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"by_size": piv.to_dict(),
         "best_overall": out.loc[out.ccc_mean.idxmax()].to_dict() if len(out) else {}},
        indent=1, default=str))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/exp2_perfold.py.text:
"""Per-participant scores behind Experiment 2's headline arms, for the appendix.

The three Experiment 2 runs report a mean and a spread per cell and throw the per-fold
values away. The appendix needs the folds themselves, so this recomputes them for the arms
that appear in the results chapter, using the same functions those runs used.

It then checks its own means against the stored ones. A per-fold table that does not
reproduce the mean it sits under would be worse than no table, so the check is the point of
the script rather than an extra.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_perfold                  # every arm
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_perfold --only alignment  # just the four arms
"""
import argparse
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from sklearn.model_selection import LeaveOneGroupOut

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from scripts.alignment_comparison.alignment_ccc import (OUT_DIM, _dcca_or_dctw_features,
                                                        _fold_predict, build_dtw_block)
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_alignment import cols_for, load, standard_model
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_crosssensor import build as build_block, load_all as load_sigs
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_fusion import SENSORS, late_fuse, oof_per_sensor
from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT
from scripts.modeling.ccc_metrics import concordance_correlation_coefficient as ccc
from scripts.utils import RANDOM_SEED

AXES = ("valence", "arousal")
WINDOWS = (5, 10, 15)
OUT_DIR = OUT / "exp2"


def folds_for(X, y, groups):
    """Per-participant CCC for one arm, keyed by participant."""
    res = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(
        delayed(_fold_predict)(standard_model(), X, y, groups, tr, te)
        for tr, te in LeaveOneGroupOut().split(X, y, groups=groups))
    return {p: float(ccc(yt, yp)) for p, _, yt, yp in res}


def alignment_folds(df, base, axis, groups, dtw_block):
    """The four alignment arms, per participant. Mirrors exp2_alignment: the fixed and
    warped arms share one feature matrix, the learned arms are fitted inside each fold."""
    y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
    out = {}
    out["fixed"] = folds_for(df[base], y, groups)
    out["dtw"] = folds_for(pd.concat([df[base], dtw_block], axis=1), y, groups)
    for method in ("dcca", "dctw"):
        vals = {}
        pids = sorted(groups.unique())
        res = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(
            delayed(_deep_fold_ccc)(df, base, y, groups, pid, i, method)
            for i, pid in enumerate(pids))
        for pid, v in res:
            vals[pid] = v
        out[method] = vals
    return out


def _deep_fold_ccc(df, base_cols, y, groups, pid, fold_i, method):
    from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_alignment import PAIRS
    train_mask = (groups != pid).to_numpy()
    extra = {}
    for m1, m2 in PAIRS:
        o = _dcca_or_dctw_features(df[train_mask], df, cols_for(df, m1), cols_for(df, m2),
                                   RANDOM_SEED + fold_i, method)
        h1, h2 = o if o is not None else (np.full((len(df), OUT_DIM), np.nan),) * 2
        for d in range(OUT_DIM):
            extra[f"{method}_{m1}-{m2}_1_{d}"] = h1[:, d]
            extra[f"{method}_{m1}-{m2}_2_{d}"] = h2[:, d]
    X = pd.concat([df[base_cols].reset_index(drop=True),
                   pd.DataFrame(extra).reset_index(drop=True)], axis=1)
    X.index = df.index
    _, _, yt, yp = _fold_predict(standard_model(), X, y, groups,
                                 np.where(train_mask)[0], np.where(~train_mask)[0])
    return pid, float(ccc(yt, yp))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--only", choices=("alignment", "rest"), default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rows = []
    for stream in ("rcea", "retro"):
        df, base = load(stream)
        groups = df["participant"]
        print(f"\n{stream}: {len(df):,} rows, {groups.nunique()} visitors", flush=True)

        if args.only != "alignment":
            sigs = load_sigs(df)
            blocks = {w: build_block(df, w, sigs) for w in WINDOWS}
            print("  cross-sensor blocks built", flush=True)
        else:
            blocks = {}
        dtw_block = build_dtw_block(df) if args.only != "rest" else None
        if dtw_block is not None:
            print("  warping block built", flush=True)

        allcols = [c for s in SENSORS for c in cols_for(df, s) if c in base]

        for axis in AXES:
            y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)

            if args.only != "rest":
                for arm, vals in alignment_folds(df, base, axis, groups, dtw_block).items():
                    for p, v in vals.items():
                        rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, arm=f"align_{arm}",
                                         participant=p, ccc=v))
                print(f"  {axis}: alignment folds done", flush=True)
            if args.only == "alignment":
                continue

            for w in WINDOWS:
                for p, v in folds_for(blocks[w], y, groups).items():
                    rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, arm=f"crosssensor_{w}s",
                                     participant=p, ccc=v))
            print(f"  {axis}: cross-sensor folds done", flush=True)

            for p, v in folds_for(df[allcols], y, groups).items():
                rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, arm="early_full",
                                 participant=p, ccc=v))
            X = pd.concat([df[allcols], blocks[5]], axis=1)
            for p, v in folds_for(X, y, groups).items():
                rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, arm="early_full_plus_block",
                                 participant=p, ccc=v))

            pred = oof_per_sensor(df, base, axis)
            for weighted, name in ((False, "late_simple_full"), (True, "late_ccc_full")):
                yh = late_fuse(pred, y, groups, tuple(SENSORS), weighted)
                for p in groups.unique():
                    m = (groups == p).to_numpy() & np.isfinite(yh)
                    if m.sum() >= 5:
                        rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, arm=name,
                                         participant=p, ccc=float(ccc(y[m], yh[m]))))
            print(f"  {axis}: fusion folds done", flush=True)

    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    path = OUT_DIR / ("exp2_perfold_alignment.csv" if args.only == "alignment"
                      else "exp2_perfold.csv")
    out.to_csv(path, index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(out)} per-participant scores written to {path}")
    if args.only == "alignment":
        al = pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / "alignment.csv")
        mine = out.groupby(["stream", "axis", "arm"]).ccc.mean()
        bad = 0
        for (st, ax, arm), v in mine.items():
            ref = al[(al.stream == st) & (al.axis == ax) & (al.arm == arm[6:])].ccc_mean
            if len(ref) and abs(v - ref.iloc[0]) > 1e-4:
                bad += 1
                print(f"  DISAGREES {st}/{ax}/{arm}: {v:+.4f} vs {ref.iloc[0]:+.4f}")
        print(f"{len(mine)} alignment cells checked, {bad} disagree")
        return

    # does the per-fold table reproduce the means the chapter already reports?
    check, fus = [], pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / "fusion.csv")
    cs = pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / "crosssensor.csv")
    mine = out.groupby(["stream", "axis", "arm"]).ccc.mean()
    for (st, ax, arm), v in mine.items():
        if arm.startswith("crosssensor_"):
            w = int(arm.split("_")[1][:-1])
            ref = cs[(cs.stream == st) & (cs.axis == ax) & (cs.window_s == w)
                     & (cs.arm == "observed")].ccc_mean
        else:
            mech = {"early_full": "early", "early_full_plus_block": "early_plus_block",
                    "late_simple_full": "late_simple", "late_ccc_full": "late_ccc"}[arm]
            g = fus[(fus.stream == st) & (fus.axis == ax) & (fus["size"] == 5)
                    & (fus.mechanism == mech)]
            ref = g.ccc_mean
        if len(ref):
            check.append(dict(stream=st, axis=ax, arm=arm, recomputed=round(float(v), 4),
                              reported=round(float(ref.iloc[0]), 4),
                              diff=round(float(v) - float(ref.iloc[0]), 5)))
    chk = pd.DataFrame(check)
    (OUT_DIR / "exp2_perfold_check.json").write_text(chk.to_json(orient="records", indent=1))
    bad = chk[chk["diff"].abs() > 1e-4]
    print(f"\n{len(chk)} cells checked against the reported means, {len(bad)} disagree")
    if len(bad):
        print(bad.to_string(index=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/exp2_repeats.py.text:
"""How much of Experiment 2's numbers is the run rather than the data.

Two questions a single run cannot answer.

How far do the headline arms move between repeats? The selection resolution of $0.08$ was
measured on one cell of Experiment 1, with a random forest on the starting configuration.
Experiment 2 uses extremely randomised trees on much wider matrices, and whether the
run-to-run spread is the same there has been assumed rather than measured.

Is the ordering of the sensor subsets stable? The result that the three mechanisms rank the
subsets alike is the one positive claim in the experiment. If the ordering is largely seed
noise, two mechanisms sharing the same per-sensor fits would agree for that reason alone.

Each repeat differs from the others exactly as the resolution's repeats did: a new seed, and
each fold's training participants resampled with replacement. Nothing else changes, so what
separates the repeats is the pipeline's own variability.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_repeats --repeats 5
"""
import argparse
import itertools
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
from sklearn.ensemble import ExtraTreesRegressor
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_alignment import cols_for, load
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_crosssensor import build as build_block, load_all as load_sigs
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_fusion import SENSORS, SHORT, late_fuse
from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT
from scripts.modeling.ccc_metrics import concordance_correlation_coefficient as ccc
from scripts.utils import RANDOM_SEED

AXES = ("valence", "arousal")
OUT_DIR = OUT / "exp2"


def model(seed):
    return Pipeline([("imp", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                     ("sc", StandardScaler()),
                     ("m", ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=300, random_state=seed, n_jobs=1))])


def _fold(X, y, tr_idx, te_idx, seed):
    pipe = model(seed)
    pipe.fit(X.iloc[tr_idx], y[tr_idx])
    return te_idx, pipe.predict(X.iloc[te_idx])


def repeat_scores(X, y, groups, seed):
    """One repeat: every fold's training participants resampled, then scored per visitor."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    pids = sorted(groups.unique())
    g = groups.to_numpy()
    jobs = []
    for o in pids:
        tr_pids = [p for p in pids if p != o]
        boot = rng.choice(tr_pids, size=len(tr_pids), replace=True)
        tr = np.where(np.isin(g, boot))[0]
        te = np.where(g == o)[0]
        if len(te) >= 5 and len(tr) > 0:
            jobs.append((tr, te))
    res = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(delayed(_fold)(X, y, tr, te, seed) for tr, te in jobs)
    vals = [ccc(y[te], yp) for te, yp in res]
    return float(np.mean(vals)) if vals else np.nan


def oof(df, base, y, groups, seed):
    """Per-sensor out-of-fold predictions for one repeat, so late fusion over any subset
    costs nothing beyond the averaging."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    pids = sorted(groups.unique())
    g = groups.to_numpy()
    pred = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=df.index, columns=list(SENSORS))
    for s in SENSORS:
        cols = [c for c in cols_for(df, s) if c in base]
        if not cols:
            continue
        X = df[cols]
        jobs = []
        for o in pids:
            tr_pids = [p for p in pids if p != o]
            boot = rng.choice(tr_pids, size=len(tr_pids), replace=True)
            jobs.append((np.where(np.isin(g, boot))[0], np.where(g == o)[0]))
        res = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(delayed(_fold)(X, y, tr, te, seed) for tr, te in jobs)
        for te, yp in res:
            pred.iloc[te, pred.columns.get_loc(s)] = yp
    return pred


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=5)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    subs = [tuple(c) for k in range(1, 6) for c in itertools.combinations(SENSORS, k)]

    head, rank = [], []
    for stream in ("rcea", "retro"):
        df, base = load(stream)
        groups = df["participant"]
        allcols = [c for s in SENSORS for c in cols_for(df, s) if c in base]
        blk = build_block(df, 5, load_sigs(df))
        Xb = pd.concat([df[allcols], blk], axis=1)
        print(f"\n{stream}: {len(df):,} rows, {groups.nunique()} visitors", flush=True)

        for axis in AXES:
            y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
            for r in range(args.repeats):
                seed = RANDOM_SEED + 1000 + r
                head.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, repeat=r, arm="early_full",
                                 ccc=repeat_scores(df[allcols], y, groups, seed)))
                head.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, repeat=r, arm="early_full_plus_block",
                                 ccc=repeat_scores(Xb, y, groups, seed)))
                pred = oof(df, base, y, groups, seed)
                for weighted, name in ((False, "late_simple_full"), (True, "late_ccc_full")):
                    yh = late_fuse(pred, y, groups, tuple(SENSORS), weighted)
                    m = np.isfinite(yh)
                    head.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, repeat=r, arm=name,
                                     ccc=float(ccc(y[m], yh[m]))))
                for sub in subs:
                    for weighted, name in ((False, "late_simple"), (True, "late_ccc")):
                        if len(sub) == 1 and weighted:
                            continue
                        yh = late_fuse(pred, y, groups, sub, weighted)
                        m = np.isfinite(yh)
                        rank.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, repeat=r, mechanism=name,
                                         subset="+".join(SHORT[s] for s in sub),
                                         size=len(sub),
                                         ccc=float(ccc(y[m], yh[m])) if m.sum() > 5 else np.nan))
                print(f"  {axis} repeat {r + 1}/{args.repeats} done", flush=True)
            pd.DataFrame(head).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "repeats_headline_partial.csv", index=False)
            pd.DataFrame(rank).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "repeats_subsets_partial.csv", index=False)

    H = pd.DataFrame(head)
    R = pd.DataFrame(rank)
    H.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "repeats_headline.csv", index=False)
    R.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "repeats_subsets.csv", index=False)

    print("\nrun-to-run spread of the headline arms, p95 minus p5 over repeats:")
    s = H.groupby(["stream", "axis", "arm"]).ccc.agg(
        lambda v: np.percentile(v, 95) - np.percentile(v, 5)).round(4)
    print(s.to_string())
    print(f"\nlargest spread {s.max():.4f}, against the resolution of 0.08")

    print("\nsubset ordering, across repeats within one mechanism:")
    within = []
    for (st, ax, mech), g in R[R["size"] > 1].groupby(["stream", "axis", "mechanism"]):
        piv = g.pivot_table(index="subset", columns="repeat", values="ccc")
        rs = [spearmanr(piv[a], piv[b]).statistic
              for a, b in itertools.combinations(piv.columns, 2)]
        within.append(dict(stream=st, axis=ax, mechanism=mech, mean_rho=float(np.mean(rs))))
    print(pd.DataFrame(within).round(2).to_string(index=False))

    print("\nsubset ordering, between the two averaging rules within one repeat:")
    between = []
    for (st, ax, rep), g in R[R["size"] > 1].groupby(["stream", "axis", "repeat"]):
        piv = g.pivot_table(index="subset", columns="mechanism", values="ccc")
        if piv.shape[1] == 2:
            between.append(spearmanr(piv.iloc[:, 0], piv.iloc[:, 1]).statistic)
    print(f"  mean rho {np.mean(between):+.2f} over {len(between)} slice-repeats")

    (OUT_DIR / "repeats_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"headline_spread": s.to_dict(),
         "max_spread": round(float(s.max()), 4),
         "within_mechanism_rho": within,
         "between_mechanism_rho": round(float(np.mean(between)), 3)}, indent=1, default=str))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/exp3_binning.py.text:
"""Experiment 3: the ordinal target and how many levels it should have.

Run in stages, because the experiment is a sequence of decisions and each one depends on
the last. Nothing is decided inside a stage that a later stage needs to revisit.

  oof       the carried matrix's out-of-fold predictions, once per slice. Both arms read
            these rows: the post-hoc arm bins them, the trained arm is fitted on the same
            matrix they came from.
  occupancy how the rated seconds fall across the levels at every count, which decides
            which counts are selectable at all, and where the scale midpoint lands.
  posthoc   the post-hoc arm across the sweep. No model is fitted at any count.
  trained   the trained-on-levels arm across the sweep. One classifier per count per fold.
  select    the arm, then the count per slice, then the jackknife on what was chosen.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp3_binning --stage oof
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp3_binning --stage occupancy
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp3_binning --stage posthoc
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp3_binning --stage trained
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp3_binning --stage select

Every stage writes its scores in full, including the per-participant values, and writes
progress to a separate file so a completed run is never overwritten by a later one.
"""
import argparse
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from sklearn.ensemble import ExtraTreesClassifier
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.metrics import balanced_accuracy_score, cohen_kappa_score
from sklearn.model_selection import LeaveOneGroupOut
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from scripts.alignment_comparison.alignment_ccc import _fold_predict
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_alignment import cols_for, load, standard_model
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_crosssensor import build as build_block, load_all as load_sigs
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_fusion import SENSORS
from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT
from scripts.utils import RANDOM_SEED

AXES = ("valence", "arousal")
COUNTS = tuple(range(3, 21))
BLOCK_WINDOW = 5
MIN_LEVEL_SHARE = 0.01      # a level holding less than this cannot be learned or scored
QWK_RESOLUTION = 0.21       # the margin in the units this experiment is scored on
OUT_DIR = OUT / "exp3"


def to_levels(y, B):
    """Equal-width levels on the known 0 to 10 scale, edges fixed by design."""
    return np.digitize(np.clip(y, 0, 10), np.linspace(0, 10, B + 1)[1:-1])


def carried_matrix(stream):
    """All five sensors' features with the cross-sensor block, the matrix Experiment 2
    carries forward."""
    df, base = load(stream)
    cols = [c for s in SENSORS for c in cols_for(df, s) if c in base]
    blk = build_block(df, BLOCK_WINDOW, load_sigs(df))
    X = pd.concat([df[cols], blk], axis=1)
    return df, X


def stage_oof(args):
    rows = []
    for stream in ("rcea", "retro"):
        df, X = carried_matrix(stream)
        groups = df["participant"]
        print(f"\n{stream}: {len(df):,} rows, {groups.nunique()} visitors, "
              f"{X.shape[1]} columns", flush=True)
        for axis in AXES:
            y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
            res = Parallel(n_jobs=args.jobs)(
                delayed(_fold_predict)(standard_model(), X, y, groups, tr, te)
                for tr, te in LeaveOneGroupOut().split(X, y, groups=groups))
            for pid, idx, yt, yp in res:
                rows += [dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, participant=pid, row=int(i),
                              y=float(a), yhat=float(b)) for i, a, b in zip(idx, yt, yp)]
            print(f"  {axis}: {len(res)} folds", flush=True)
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "oof_carried.csv", index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(out):,} out-of-fold predictions written")


def stage_occupancy(args):
    rows = []
    for stream in ("rcea", "retro"):
        df, _ = load(stream)
        for axis in AXES:
            y = df[axis].dropna().to_numpy()
            for B in COUNTS:
                lv = to_levels(y, B)
                share = np.bincount(lv, minlength=B) / len(lv)
                edges = np.linspace(0, 10, B + 1)
                rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, B=B,
                                 min_share=float(share.min()),
                                 max_share=float(share.max()),
                                 levels_under_1pct=int((share < MIN_LEVEL_SHARE).sum()),
                                 midpoint_share=float(np.mean(np.isclose(y, 5.0, atol=1e-6))),
                                 midpoint_on_edge=bool(np.isclose(edges, 5.0).any())))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    sel = out.groupby("B").min_share.min() >= MIN_LEVEL_SHARE
    out["selectable"] = out.B.map(sel)
    out.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "occupancy.csv", index=False)
    print("count  emptiest level over all four slices  selectable")
    for B in COUNTS:
        g = out[out.B == B]
        print(f"{B:>5}  {g.min_share.min() * 100:>34.2f}%  {'yes' if sel[B] else 'no'}")
    print(f"\nselectable counts: {[int(b) for b in sel.index[sel]]}")


def score_binned(y_true_lv, y_pred_lv, B):
    labels = list(range(B))
    return (float(cohen_kappa_score(y_true_lv, y_pred_lv, weights="quadratic", labels=labels)),
            float(balanced_accuracy_score(y_true_lv, y_pred_lv)))


def stage_posthoc(args):
    oof = pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / "oof_carried.csv")
    rows, folds = [], []
    for (stream, axis), g in oof.groupby(["stream", "axis"]):
        for B in COUNTS:
            t, p = to_levels(g.y.to_numpy(), B), to_levels(g.yhat.to_numpy(), B)
            qwk, ba = score_binned(t, p, B)
            rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, B=B, arm="posthoc",
                             qwk=qwk, balanced_accuracy=ba, chance=1 / B,
                             rows=len(g), folds=g.participant.nunique()))
            for pid, h in g.groupby("participant"):
                tt, pp = to_levels(h.y.to_numpy(), B), to_levels(h.yhat.to_numpy(), B)
                if len(tt) >= 5:
                    folds.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, B=B, arm="posthoc",
                                      participant=pid,
                                      qwk=float(cohen_kappa_score(tt, pp, weights="quadratic",
                                                                  labels=list(range(B))))))
        print(f"  {stream}/{axis}: swept {len(COUNTS)} counts", flush=True)
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "sweep_posthoc.csv", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(folds).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "sweep_posthoc_perfold.csv", index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(rows)} cells, {len(folds)} per-participant scores")


def _fit_fold(X, ylv, groups, tr, te, B):
    pipe = Pipeline([("imp", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                     ("sc", StandardScaler()),
                     ("m", ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=300, random_state=RANDOM_SEED,
                                                n_jobs=1))])
    pipe.fit(X.iloc[tr], ylv[tr])
    return groups.iloc[te].iloc[0], ylv[te], pipe.predict(X.iloc[te])


def stage_trained(args):
    rows, folds = [], []
    for stream in ("rcea", "retro"):
        df, X = carried_matrix(stream)
        groups = df["participant"]
        print(f"\n{stream}: {X.shape[1]} columns", flush=True)
        for axis in AXES:
            y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
            splits = list(LeaveOneGroupOut().split(X, y, groups=groups))
            for B in COUNTS:
                ylv = to_levels(y, B)
                res = Parallel(n_jobs=args.jobs)(
                    delayed(_fit_fold)(X, ylv, groups, tr, te, B) for tr, te in splits)
                t = np.concatenate([r[1] for r in res])
                p = np.concatenate([r[2] for r in res])
                qwk, ba = score_binned(t, p, B)
                rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, B=B, arm="trained",
                                 qwk=qwk, balanced_accuracy=ba, chance=1 / B,
                                 rows=len(t), folds=len(res)))
                for pid, tt, pp in res:
                    if len(tt) >= 5:
                        folds.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, B=B, arm="trained",
                                          participant=pid,
                                          qwk=float(cohen_kappa_score(
                                              tt, pp, weights="quadratic",
                                              labels=list(range(B))))))
                print(f"  {axis} B={B:<2} QWK {qwk:+.4f}  BA {ba:.4f} (chance {1/B:.3f})",
                      flush=True)
                pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "sweep_trained_partial.csv", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "sweep_trained.csv", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(folds).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "sweep_trained_perfold.csv", index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(rows)} cells, {len(folds)} per-participant scores")


def stage_select(args):
    """The arm, then the count, then the jackknife on what was chosen.

    The arm is summarised by the mean of its best selectable pooled QWK over the four slices.
    The count is then read per slice on pooled QWK alone. The jackknife repeats the comparison
    among the candidate counts with each visitor held out in turn, recomputed from the stored
    per-participant scores rather than by refitting, and reports how often the same count still
    comes first.
    """
    occ = pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / "occupancy.csv")
    sel = sorted(int(b) for b in occ.groupby("B").min_share.min()
                 .loc[lambda s: s >= MIN_LEVEL_SHARE].index)
    print(f"selectable counts: {sel}")

    arms, peaks = {}, {}
    for name in ("posthoc", "trained"):
        d = pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / f"sweep_{name}.csv")
        d = d[d.B.isin(sel)]
        arms[name] = float(d.qwk.mean())          # over the selectable counts and the slices
        by_count = d.groupby("B").qwk.mean()
        peaks[name] = (int(by_count.idxmax()), float(by_count.max()))
        print(f"  {name:8s} mean pooled QWK over the selectable counts {arms[name]:+.4f}, "
              f"peaking at {peaks[name][0]} levels at {peaks[name][1]:+.4f}")
    gap = abs(arms["trained"] - arms["posthoc"])
    carried = "trained"
    print(f"  difference {gap:.4f} against the margin of {QWK_RESOLUTION}; "
          f"carrying the {carried} arm"
          f"{' (tied)' if gap < QWK_RESOLUTION else ''}")

    rows = []
    sweep = pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / f"sweep_{carried}.csv")
    folds = pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / f"sweep_{carried}_perfold.csv")
    for stream in ("rcea", "retro"):
        for axis in AXES:
            g = sweep[(sweep.stream == stream) & (sweep.axis == axis) & (sweep.B.isin(sel))]
            best = g.loc[g.qwk.idxmax()]
            tied = sorted(int(b) for b in g[g.qwk >= best.qwk - QWK_RESOLUTION].B)
            chosen = min(tied)                      # the coarsest of the tied counts
            piv = (folds[(folds.stream == stream) & (folds.axis == axis)
                         & (folds.B.isin(sel))]
                   .pivot_table(index="participant", columns="B", values="qwk"))
            winner = int(piv.mean(axis=0).idxmax())
            same = sum(1 for p in piv.index
                       if int(piv.drop(index=p).mean(axis=0).idxmax()) == winner)
            rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, arm=carried,
                             best_count=int(best.B), best_qwk=float(best.qwk),
                             tied_counts=",".join(str(b) for b in tied),
                             span=float(g.qwk.max() - g.qwk.min()),
                             carried_count=chosen,
                             jackknife_winner=winner, jackknife_stable=same,
                             jackknife_folds=len(piv),
                             jackknife_pct=round(100 * same / len(piv), 1)))
            r = rows[-1]
            print(f"  {stream:6s} {axis:8s} best B={r['best_count']} at {r['best_qwk']:+.4f}, "
                  f"span {r['span']:.4f}, tied {r['tied_counts']}, carried B={chosen}, "
                  f"jackknife {r['jackknife_pct']:.0f}% on B={winner}", flush=True)
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "selection.csv", index=False)
    (OUT_DIR / "selection_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"selectable_counts": sel, "arm_means": arms, "arm_peaks": peaks,
         "arm_gap": round(gap, 4), "carried_arm": carried,
         "carried_count": {f"{r.stream}/{r.axis}": int(r.carried_count)
                           for r in out.itertuples()}}, indent=1))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True,
                    choices=("oof", "occupancy", "posthoc", "trained", "select"))
    ap.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=-1)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    {"oof": stage_oof, "occupancy": stage_occupancy, "posthoc": stage_posthoc,
     "trained": stage_trained, "select": stage_select}[args.stage](args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/exp4_localisation.py.text:
"""Experiment 4: does scoping prediction to the attended painting recover more affect?

Two models are compared. The first is the one Experiments 2 and 3 already carry, trained on
whole sessions. The second is fitted here on the attended rows alone. Each held-out visitor
is scored under both, and in both cases the rows scored are that visitor's attended rows.

Three quantities come out of the two models, so the training rows and the scored rows move
one at a time:

  whole_session      trained on whole sessions, scored on the whole session. Context only.
  whole_on_attended  the same model's held-out predictions, scored on attended rows alone.
  attended_trained   trained on attended rows, scored on attended rows.

The comparison that answers the question is whole_on_attended against attended_trained:
identical scored rows, so the only difference is what the model learned from.

Run in stages, because each one depends on the last.

  labels     the attended-painting label for every analysed second, cached once.
  scoping    the three quantities pooled over all five paintings, on all three metrics.
  perpainting the same three quantities within each painting on its own.
  tests      the paired tests with false-discovery control, per metric family.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp4_localisation --stage labels
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp4_localisation --stage scoping
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp4_localisation --stage perpainting
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp4_localisation --stage tests

Every stage writes its per-participant scores in full, and writes progress to a separate
file so a completed run is never overwritten by a later one.
"""
import argparse
import json
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from scipy.stats import wilcoxon
from sklearn.ensemble import ExtraTreesClassifier
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.metrics import balanced_accuracy_score, cohen_kappa_score
from sklearn.model_selection import LeaveOneGroupOut
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from scripts.alignment_comparison.alignment_ccc import _fold_predict
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_alignment import standard_model
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp3_binning import carried_matrix, to_levels
from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT
from scripts.modeling.ccc_metrics import concordance_correlation_coefficient as ccc
from scripts.thesis_v2.attention_labels import attended_painting_at_timepoints
from scripts.utils import RANDOM_SEED

AXES = ("valence", "arousal")
STREAMS = ("rcea", "retro")
PAINTINGS = ("B1", "B2", "B3", "C5", "C6")
LEVELS = 3                  # the count Experiment 3 carries on every slice
MIN_PARTICIPANTS = 5        # a cell below either threshold is recorded as not reportable
MIN_ROWS = 50
MIN_FOLD_ROWS = 5           # a fold below this cannot carry a per-participant score
OUT_DIR = OUT / "exp4"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- attended labels

def stage_labels(args):
    """The attended painting for every analysed second, cached so the later stages do not
    pay for the interval arithmetic again."""
    rows = []
    for stream in STREAMS:
        df, _ = carried_matrix(stream)
        for pid, g in df.groupby("participant"):
            lab = attended_painting_at_timepoints(pid, pd.DatetimeIndex(g["utc"]))
            rows += [dict(stream=stream, participant=pid, row=int(i), painting=p)
                     for i, p in zip(g.index, lab.to_numpy()) if isinstance(p, str)]
        n = sum(1 for r in rows if r["stream"] == stream)
        print(f"{stream}: {n:,} attended seconds of {len(df):,} "
              f"({100 * n / len(df):.1f}%)", flush=True)
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "attended_labels.csv", index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(out):,} labelled seconds written")
    print(out.groupby(["stream", "painting"]).size().to_string())


def load_labels(stream):
    lab = pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / "attended_labels.csv")
    return lab[lab.stream == stream]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the two models

def _fit_classifier_fold(X, ylv, groups, tr, te):
    pipe = Pipeline([("imp", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                     ("sc", StandardScaler()),
                     ("m", ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=300, random_state=RANDOM_SEED,
                                                n_jobs=1))])
    pipe.fit(X.iloc[tr], ylv[tr])
    return groups.iloc[te].iloc[0], np.asarray(te), ylv[te], pipe.predict(X.iloc[te])


def oof_predictions(X, y, groups, jobs):
    """Held-out predictions from both models on the rows given, under one leave-one-visitor-out
    pass each. Returns the continuous prediction and the level prediction on the same rows."""
    ylv = to_levels(y, LEVELS)
    splits = [(tr, te) for tr, te in LeaveOneGroupOut().split(X, y, groups=groups)
              if len(te) >= MIN_FOLD_ROWS and len(np.unique(ylv[tr])) > 1]
    reg = Parallel(n_jobs=jobs)(
        delayed(_fold_predict)(standard_model(), X, y, groups, tr, te) for tr, te in splits)
    clf = Parallel(n_jobs=jobs)(
        delayed(_fit_classifier_fold)(X, ylv, groups, tr, te) for tr, te in splits)
    pos = np.concatenate([np.asarray(te) for _, te in splits])
    out = pd.DataFrame(dict(
        pos=pos,
        participant=np.concatenate([[p] * len(t) for (p, _, t, _), (_, te) in zip(reg, splits)]),
        y=np.concatenate([t for _, _, t, _ in reg]),
        yhat=np.concatenate([p for _, _, _, p in reg]),
        ylv=np.concatenate([t for _, _, t, _ in clf]),
        ylv_hat=np.concatenate([p for _, _, _, p in clf])))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scoring

def score_cell(pred, tag):
    """Every metric a quantity is read on, with the per-participant values behind them.

    CCC is the mean of the per-visitor values, as in Experiments 1 and 2. QWK is pooled once
    over every held-out prediction, as in Experiment 3, with balanced accuracy beside it.
    """
    if pred.empty:
        return None, []
    labels = list(range(LEVELS))
    folds, ccc_vals, qwk_vals = [], [], []
    for pid, g in pred.groupby("participant"):
        if len(g) < MIN_FOLD_ROWS:
            continue
        c = float(ccc(g.y.to_numpy(), g.yhat.to_numpy()))
        q = (float(cohen_kappa_score(g.ylv, g.ylv_hat, weights="quadratic", labels=labels))
             if g.ylv.nunique() > 1 or g.ylv_hat.nunique() > 1 else np.nan)
        ccc_vals.append(c)
        if np.isfinite(q):
            qwk_vals.append(q)
        folds.append(dict(participant=pid, rows=len(g), ccc=c, qwk=q))
    if not ccc_vals:
        return None, []
    cell = dict(
        rows=len(pred), participants=pred.participant.nunique(),
        ccc_mean=float(np.mean(ccc_vals)), ccc_sd=float(np.std(ccc_vals)),
        ccc_folds=len(ccc_vals),
        qwk_pooled=float(cohen_kappa_score(pred.ylv, pred.ylv_hat,
                                           weights="quadratic", labels=labels)),
        qwk_mean=float(np.mean(qwk_vals)) if qwk_vals else np.nan,
        qwk_folds=len(qwk_vals),
        balanced_accuracy=float(balanced_accuracy_score(pred.ylv, pred.ylv_hat)),
        chance=1 / LEVELS)
    cell["reportable"] = bool(cell["participants"] >= MIN_PARTICIPANTS
                              and cell["rows"] >= MIN_ROWS)
    return cell, folds


_MATRIX = {}
_WHOLE = {}


def _matrix(stream):
    """The carried matrix, built once per stream. Rebuilding it per painting would recompute
    the cross-sensor block five times over for no change in its contents."""
    if stream not in _MATRIX:
        _MATRIX[stream] = carried_matrix(stream)
    return _MATRIX[stream]


def quantities(stream, axis, jobs, painting=None):
    """The three quantities for one slice, optionally within one painting.

    The whole-session model is fitted once on every row. Its predictions are then read twice,
    on the whole session and on the attended rows alone. The attended-trained model is a
    separate fit on the attended rows only.

    The whole-session fit does not depend on which painting is being looked at, so it is
    computed once per slice and reused across the five paintings.
    """
    df, X = _matrix(stream)
    y = df[axis].to_numpy(float)
    groups = df["participant"]

    lab = load_labels(stream)
    if painting is not None:
        lab = lab[lab.painting == painting]
    keep = np.zeros(len(df), bool)
    keep[lab.row.to_numpy()] = True

    if (stream, axis) not in _WHOLE:
        _WHOLE[(stream, axis)] = oof_predictions(X, y, groups, jobs)
    whole = _WHOLE[(stream, axis)]
    att_mask = keep[whole.pos.to_numpy()]
    out = {"whole_session": whole, "whole_on_attended": whole[att_mask]}

    idx = np.where(keep)[0]
    if len(idx) >= MIN_ROWS and groups.iloc[idx].nunique() >= 2:
        Xa, ya, ga = X.iloc[idx], y[idx], groups.iloc[idx].reset_index(drop=True)
        at = oof_predictions(Xa.reset_index(drop=True), ya, ga, jobs)
        at["pos"] = idx[at.pos.to_numpy()]
        out["attended_trained"] = at
    else:
        out["attended_trained"] = whole.iloc[0:0]
    return out


def _run(scope, jobs, painting=None):
    cells, folds = [], []
    for stream in STREAMS:
        for axis in AXES:
            q = quantities(stream, axis, jobs, painting)
            for name, pred in q.items():
                cell, f = score_cell(pred, name)
                if cell is None:
                    cells.append(dict(scope=scope, painting=painting or "all", stream=stream,
                                      axis=axis, quantity=name, rows=len(pred),
                                      participants=0, reportable=False))
                    continue
                cells.append(dict(scope=scope, painting=painting or "all", stream=stream,
                                  axis=axis, quantity=name, **cell))
                for r in f:
                    folds.append(dict(scope=scope, painting=painting or "all", stream=stream,
                                      axis=axis, quantity=name, **r))
            print(f"  {stream}/{axis} {painting or 'pooled':>6}: "
                  + "  ".join(f"{k.split('_')[0]} {v['ccc_mean']:+.4f}"
                              for k, v in zip(q, [c for c in cells[-len(q):]])
                              if "ccc_mean" in v), flush=True)
    return pd.DataFrame(cells), pd.DataFrame(folds)


def stage_scoping(args):
    cells, folds = _run("pooled", args.jobs)
    cells.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "scoping.csv", index=False)
    folds.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "scoping_perfold.csv", index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(cells)} cells, {len(folds)} per-participant scores")
    print(cells[["stream", "axis", "quantity", "rows", "participants",
                 "ccc_mean", "qwk_pooled", "balanced_accuracy"]].to_string(index=False))


def stage_perpainting(args):
    allc, allf = [], []
    for p in PAINTINGS:
        print(f"\n=== {p} ===", flush=True)
        c, f = _run("painting", args.jobs, p)
        allc.append(c)
        allf.append(f)
        pd.concat(allc).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "perpainting_partial.csv", index=False)
    cells, folds = pd.concat(allc, ignore_index=True), pd.concat(allf, ignore_index=True)
    cells.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "perpainting.csv", index=False)
    folds.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "perpainting_perfold.csv", index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(cells)} cells, {len(folds)} per-participant scores")
    print(f"reportable: {int(cells.reportable.sum())} of {len(cells)}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- testing

def bh(p):
    """Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values, in the order given."""
    p = np.asarray(p, float)
    ok = np.isfinite(p)
    q = np.full(len(p), np.nan)
    v = p[ok]
    if not len(v):
        return q
    order = np.argsort(v)
    ranked = v[order] * len(v) / (np.arange(len(v)) + 1)
    ranked = np.minimum.accumulate(ranked[::-1])[::-1]
    adj = np.empty(len(v))
    adj[order] = np.clip(ranked, 0, 1)
    q[ok] = adj
    return q


def stage_tests(args):
    """Paired tests over per-participant scores, corrected inside each metric's own family.

    The family spans the paintings, the two streams and the two axes, which is the set of
    comparisons this experiment makes.
    """
    folds = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / "scoping_perfold.csv"),
                       pd.read_csv(OUT_DIR / "perpainting_perfold.csv")], ignore_index=True)
    pairs = [("whole_on_attended", "attended_trained"),
             ("whole_session", "whole_on_attended")]
    rows = []
    for a, b in pairs:
        for (painting, stream, axis), g in folds.groupby(["painting", "stream", "axis"]):
            wide = g.pivot_table(index="participant", columns="quantity",
                                 values=["ccc", "qwk"])
            for metric in ("ccc", "qwk"):
                if (metric, a) not in wide.columns or (metric, b) not in wide.columns:
                    continue
                d = wide[[(metric, a), (metric, b)]].dropna()
                if len(d) < MIN_PARTICIPANTS:
                    continue
                x, z = d[(metric, a)].to_numpy(), d[(metric, b)].to_numpy()
                if np.allclose(x, z):
                    stat, p = np.nan, 1.0
                else:
                    stat, p = wilcoxon(x, z)
                rows.append(dict(comparison=f"{a}_vs_{b}", metric=metric, painting=painting,
                                 stream=stream, axis=axis, n=len(d),
                                 mean_a=float(x.mean()), mean_b=float(z.mean()),
                                 delta=float(z.mean() - x.mean()),
                                 improved=int((z > x).sum()), p=float(p)))
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if t.empty:
        raise SystemExit("no testable comparisons")
    t["q"] = np.nan
    for metric, g in t.groupby("metric"):
        t.loc[g.index, "q"] = bh(g.p.to_numpy())
    t["significant"] = t.q < 0.05
    t.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "tests.csv", index=False)
    print(t.to_string(index=False))
    print(f"\n{int(t.significant.sum())} of {len(t)} comparisons survive correction")
    (OUT_DIR / "tests_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"n_tests": len(t), "n_significant": int(t.significant.sum()),
         "by_metric": {m: int(g.significant.sum()) for m, g in t.groupby("metric")}}, indent=1))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True,
                    choices=("labels", "scoping", "perpainting", "tests"))
    ap.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=-1)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    {"labels": stage_labels, "scoping": stage_scoping,
     "perpainting": stage_perpainting, "tests": stage_tests}[args.stage](args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/exp4_variance.py.text:
"""Experiment 4's variance decomposition: where a rating's variance actually sits.

Every attended second carries three things: the rating, the visitor who produced it, and the
painting they were attending. A crossed mixed-effects model splits the spread in those
ratings into the share belonging to the visitor, the share belonging to the painting, and the
residual belonging to neither.

The estimators are not reimplemented here. The crossed REML fit, the participant-cluster
bootstrap, the leave-one-painting-out refit and the one-way eta-squared cross-check all come
from the characterisation modules, which already handle the two statsmodels traps that would
otherwise give silently wrong numbers: `res.vcomp` is already in response-variance units, and
it is ordered alphabetically rather than by insertion. What changes here is only the data
those estimators are given, which is this chapter's carried matrix on the attended rows the
percentile proximity rule defines.

  ratings   the split of each slice's ratings, with all three checks around it.
  sensors   the same split on every carried feature, rolled up to the five sensor categories,
            with degenerate fits counted and excluded.
  binned    the same split on the level index, to show whether discretising moves the shares.
  icc       the painting share recomputed on one mean rating per visitor per painting. With
            paintings as targets and visitors as raters that quantity is ICC(2,1), absolute
            agreement, single rater, which is the form the agreement literature reports.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp4_variance --stage ratings
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp4_variance --stage sensors
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp4_variance --stage binned
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp4_variance --stage icc
"""
import argparse
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from scripts.characterization.mixed_effects_variance import (
    _cluster_bootstrap_ci, _crossed_varcomp, _jackknife_painting,
    crossed_varcomp_with_fallback)
from scripts.characterization.variance_decomposition import _eta2
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_alignment import cols_for
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp2_fusion import SENSORS
from scripts.exp1_v2.exp3_binning import carried_matrix, to_levels
from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT

AXES = ("valence", "arousal")
STREAMS = ("rcea", "retro")
LEVELS = 3
MIN_ROWS = 50
OUT_DIR = OUT / "exp4"
LABELS = OUT_DIR / "attended_labels.csv"

# A crossed fit whose person or painting component reaches the boundary has not split the
# variance: the surviving component absorbs what the collapsed one should have held, and the
# resulting share describes that collapse rather than the feature. Such fits are recorded and
# left out of a category's mean. The rule and the threshold are the previous generation's,
# whose module cannot be imported because it reads result files that no longer exist.
REML_BOUNDARY_PCT = 0.05


def reml_feature_split(d: pd.DataFrame, col: str) -> dict:
    """The crossed split of one column, with the degeneracy guard."""
    out = {"painting_reml_pct": np.nan, "person_reml_pct": np.nan,
           "residual_reml_pct": np.nan, "reml_converged": False, "reml_degenerate": True}
    dd = d.dropna(subset=[col])
    if len(dd) < MIN_ROWS or dd["participant"].nunique() < 3 or dd["painting"].nunique() < 2:
        return out
    try:
        r = _crossed_varcomp(dd, col)
    except Exception:
        return out
    degenerate = (r["me_between_person_pct"] < REML_BOUNDARY_PCT
                  or r["me_between_painting_pct"] < REML_BOUNDARY_PCT)
    return {"painting_reml_pct": r["me_between_painting_pct"],
            "person_reml_pct": r["me_between_person_pct"],
            "residual_reml_pct": r["me_residual_pct"],
            "reml_converged": bool(r["converged"]),
            "reml_degenerate": bool(degenerate or not r["converged"])}


def attended(stream):
    """The attended rows of one stream, as the frame the estimators expect: a participant
    column, a painting column, both axes, and this chapter's carried features."""
    df, X = carried_matrix(stream)
    lab = pd.read_csv(LABELS)
    lab = lab[lab.stream == stream].set_index("row")
    idx = lab.index.to_numpy()
    d = pd.concat([df.loc[idx, ["participant", *AXES]], X.loc[idx]], axis=1)
    d["painting"] = lab.loc[idx, "painting"].to_numpy()
    return d.reset_index(drop=True), list(X.columns)


def _category(col):
    """The sensor a carried column belongs to. The cross-sensor block is its own category:
    it is built from three signals at once and belongs to none of them."""
    for s in SENSORS:
        if col.startswith(f"{s}__"):
            return s
    return "cross_sensor"


def stage_ratings(args):
    rows = []
    for stream in STREAMS:
        d, _ = attended(stream)
        for axis in AXES:
            me = crossed_varcomp_with_fallback(d, axis, label=f"{stream}/{axis}")
            ci = _cluster_bootstrap_ci(d, axis, n_boot=args.boot)
            jack = _jackknife_painting(d, axis)
            rows.append(dict(
                stream=stream, axis=axis, target="rating",
                n_rows=int(len(d.dropna(subset=[axis]))),
                n_participants=int(d.participant.nunique()),
                n_paintings=int(d.painting.nunique()), **me,
                eta2_person_pct=round(100 * _eta2(d, "participant", axis), 2),
                eta2_painting_pct=round(100 * _eta2(d, "painting", axis), 2),
                **ci, **jack))
            r = rows[-1]
            print(f"[{stream}/{axis}] person {r['me_between_person_pct']}%  "
                  f"painting {r['me_between_painting_pct']}%  "
                  f"residual {r['me_residual_pct']}%  | painting 95% CI "
                  f"[{r['me_painting_ci_lo']}, {r['me_painting_ci_hi']}]  "
                  f"jackknife [{r['me_painting_jack_min']}, {r['me_painting_jack_max']}]  "
                  f"eta2 painting {r['eta2_painting_pct']}%  "
                  f"(boot {r['n_boot_converged']}/{args.boot})", flush=True)
            pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "variance_ratings_partial.csv", index=False)
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "variance_ratings.csv", index=False)
    tot = out[["me_between_person_pct", "me_between_painting_pct", "me_residual_pct"]].sum(axis=1)
    print(f"\nshares sum to {tot.min():.1f} to {tot.max():.1f} per cent across the four slices")


def stage_binned(args):
    """The same split on the level index, on identical rows, so the continuous and the
    discretised shares can be read side by side."""
    rows = []
    for stream in STREAMS:
        d, _ = attended(stream)
        for axis in AXES:
            dd = d.copy()
            dd[axis] = to_levels(d[axis].to_numpy(float), LEVELS).astype(float)
            me = crossed_varcomp_with_fallback(dd, axis, label=f"{stream}/{axis}/binned")
            rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, target=f"level_{LEVELS}",
                             n_rows=int(len(dd.dropna(subset=[axis]))),
                             n_participants=int(dd.participant.nunique()),
                             n_paintings=int(dd.painting.nunique()), **me,
                             eta2_person_pct=round(100 * _eta2(dd, "participant", axis), 2),
                             eta2_painting_pct=round(100 * _eta2(dd, "painting", axis), 2)))
            r = rows[-1]
            print(f"[{stream}/{axis}] binned: person {r['me_between_person_pct']}%  "
                  f"painting {r['me_between_painting_pct']}%  "
                  f"residual {r['me_residual_pct']}%", flush=True)
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "variance_binned.csv", index=False)


def stage_icc(args):
    """The painting share on one mean rating per visitor per painting.

    At one observation per visitor-painting cell the crossed split is ICC(2,1) with paintings
    as targets and visitors as raters, which is the inter-visitor agreement coefficient in its
    usual form. Reported beside the second-level split, whose residual also absorbs the
    movement within a painting and which is therefore the lower of the two.
    """
    rows = []
    for stream in STREAMS:
        d, _ = attended(stream)
        for axis in AXES:
            cell = (d.groupby(["participant", "painting"], as_index=False)[axis].mean())
            me = crossed_varcomp_with_fallback(cell, axis, label=f"{stream}/{axis}/means")
            rows.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, target="painting_mean",
                             n_cells=int(len(cell)),
                             n_participants=int(cell.participant.nunique()),
                             n_paintings=int(cell.painting.nunique()), **me,
                             icc_painting_as_target=me["me_between_painting_pct"] / 100,
                             icc_person_as_target=me["me_between_person_pct"] / 100))
            r = rows[-1]
            print(f"[{stream}/{axis}] on {r['n_cells']} visitor-painting means: "
                  f"painting {r['me_between_painting_pct']}%  "
                  f"person {r['me_between_person_pct']}%  "
                  f"residual {r['me_residual_pct']}%  "
                  f"(ICC paintings-as-targets {r['icc_painting_as_target']:+.4f})", flush=True)
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT_DIR / "variance_icc.csv", index=False)


def stage_sensors(args):
    """Every carried column through the identical procedure, rolled up to the sensor
    categories. A fit whose person or painting component collapses to the boundary has not
    split the variance, so it is recorded as degenerate and left out of its category's mean.
    """
    feat_rows = []
    for stream in STREAMS:
        d, cols = attended(stream)
        if args.limit:
            cols = cols[:args.limit]
        print(f"\n=== {stream}: {len(cols)} columns ===", flush=True)
        for i, col in enumerate(cols, 1):
            r = reml_feature_split(d, col)
            feat_rows.append(dict(stream=stream, feature=col, category=_category(col),
                                  eta2_painting_pct=round(100 * _eta2(d, "painting", col), 2),
                                  eta2_person_pct=round(100 * _eta2(d, "participant", col), 2),
                                  **r))
            if i % 20 == 0 or i == len(cols):
                print(f"  {i}/{len(cols)}", flush=True)
                pd.DataFrame(feat_rows).to_csv(
                    OUT_DIR / "variance_features_partial.csv", index=False)
    feats = pd.DataFrame(feat_rows)
    feats.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "variance_features.csv", index=False)

    ok = feats[~feats.reml_degenerate]
    roll = (ok.groupby(["stream", "category"])
            .agg(painting_pct=("painting_reml_pct", "mean"),
                 person_pct=("person_reml_pct", "mean"),
                 residual_pct=("residual_reml_pct", "mean"),
                 eta2_painting_pct=("eta2_painting_pct", "mean"),
                 n_features=("feature", "count")).reset_index())
    counts = feats.groupby(["stream", "category"]).agg(
        n_total=("feature", "count"), n_degenerate=("reml_degenerate", "sum")).reset_index()
    roll = roll.merge(counts, on=["stream", "category"], how="right").round(3)
    roll.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "variance_sensors.csv", index=False)
    print("\n" + roll.to_string(index=False))
    print(f"\n{int(feats.reml_degenerate.sum())} of {len(feats)} feature fits degenerate "
          f"at the {REML_BOUNDARY_PCT}% boundary")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True,
                    choices=("ratings", "sensors", "binned", "icc"))
    ap.add_argument("--boot", type=int, default=500)
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0,
                    help="first N columns only, for timing the per-feature stage")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    {"ratings": stage_ratings, "sensors": stage_sensors,
     "binned": stage_binned, "icc": stage_icc}[args.stage](args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/exp5_personalisation.py.text:
"""Experiment 5: does personalising the visitor-general model recover person-specific structure?

Three levers, differing in what they adapt.

  baseline          the features. Each visitor's own resting level, taken as the median of
                    each feature over the seconds before they first attended a painting, is
                    subtracted from every row of that visitor's session. Fitted per person
                    from features alone, so it uses no rating from anyone and can be run on
                    a visitor the system has never met.
  warmup_{N}        the training data. The opening N seconds of the held-out visitor's own
                    annotated stream are appended to the population model's training set,
                    unweighted, and the model is refitted. Swept at 30, 60, 120 and 180 s.
  person_relative   the target. Level boundaries are placed at equal-frequency positions in
                    a visitor's own ratings rather than at the same absolute position for
                    everyone. Training visitors use their full session, the held-out visitor
                    the opening slice alone.

Every lever and its reference is scored on one common set of rows per visitor: those left
once both the baseline window and the longest warm-up have been set aside. That makes every
figure comparable to every other, not only to its own reference.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp5_personalisation --stage rows
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp5_personalisation --stage levers
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.exp5_personalisation --stage tests
"""
import argparse
import json
import warnings
