"""Write the pipeline-configuration summary from the stored selections.

One table. Every choice the chapter made, what it was chosen against, what the margin was,
and whether the candidates could be told apart at all. A reader who wants to know what the
carried pipeline actually is should be able to read it off one page rather than assemble it
from five experiments.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.make_supplementary_appendix
"""
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT

TEX = "/Users/akshaj/Documents/Thesis/research-proposal/appendix_final_supplementary.tex"


def load(path, default=None):
    p = OUT / path
    if not p.is_file():
        return default
    return json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.suffix == ".json" else pd.read_csv(p)


def rows():
    """Each row: the decision, what was carried, the runners-up, the span, and the margin."""
    out = []

    res = load("resolution.json", {})
    resq = load("resolution_qwk.json", {})
    rc = res.get("resolution", float("nan"))
    rq = resq.get("resolution_qwk", float("nan"))

    out.append(("Experiment 1", "Selection resolution, \\ac{CCC}",
                f"${rc:.2f}$", "20 repeats on one cell", "", ""))
    out.append(("Experiment 1", "Selection resolution, pooled \\ac{QWK}",
                f"${rq:.2f}$", "20 repeats on the same cell", "", ""))
    out.append(("Experiment 1", "Fixation rule", "30 degrees per second",
                "adaptive, \\ac{IDT}, 240 deg/s", "", f"${rc:.2f}$"))
    out.append(("Experiment 1", "Pupil diameter", "uncorrected",
                "gaze-angle corrected", "", f"${rc:.2f}$"))
    out.append(("Experiment 1", "Window delay, pupil and \\ac{HRV}", "trailing, no delay",
                "trailing and forward, zero to six seconds", "", f"${rc:.2f}$"))
    out.append(("Experiment 1", "Interbeat multiplier", "3", "4, 5", "", f"${rc:.2f}$"))
    out.append(("Experiment 1", "Electrodermal decomposition", "NeuroKit, 3\\,s window",
                "12\\,s window, other decompositions", "", f"${rc:.2f}$"))

    import glob
    cells = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f) for f in sorted(glob.glob(str(OUT / "families/cell_*.csv")))])
    permodel = (cells.groupby(["stream", "sensor", "axis", "family"])["ccc"].mean()
                .reset_index().groupby("family")["ccc"].mean())
    nfam = len(permodel)
    span = permodel.max() - permodel.min()
    out.append(("Experiment 1", "Model family", "extremely randomised trees",
                f"{nfam - 1} other families", f"${span:.4f}$", f"${rc:.2f}$"))

    al = load("exp2/alignment_summary.json", {})
    per = al.get("per_arm_mean_ccc", {})
    if per:
        others = ", ".join(k for k in per if k != "fixed")
        out.append(("Experiment 2", "Alignment method", "fixed windowing", others,
                    f"${al.get('spread', float('nan')):.4f}$", f"${rc:.2f}$"))

    cs = load("exp2/crosssensor.csv")
    if cs is not None:
        obs = cs[cs.arm == "observed"].groupby("window_s").ccc_mean.mean()
        out.append(("Experiment 2", "Cross-sensor window", "5\\,s", "10\\,s, 15\\,s",
                    f"${obs.max() - obs.min():.4f}$", f"${rc:.2f}$"))

    fu = load("exp2/fusion.csv")
    ba = load("exp2/fusion_block_arms.csv")
    if fu is not None and ba is not None:
        full = "P+E+H+Sa+Sc"
        m = {k: v for k, v in
             fu[fu.subset == full].groupby("mechanism").ccc_mean.mean().items()}
        m["early_plus_block"] = float(ba[ba.subset == full].ccc_mean.mean())
        span = max(m.values()) - min(m.values())
        out.append(("Experiment 2", "Combination mechanism",
                    "early fusion with the cross-sensor block",
                    "early fusion, weighted and simple averaging",
                    f"${span:.4f}$", f"${rc:.2f}$"))

    sel = load("exp3/selection_summary.json", {})
    if sel:
        out.append(("Experiment 3", "Ordinal arm", "trained on levels", "post-hoc binning",
                    f"${sel.get('arm_gap', float('nan')):.4f}$", f"${rq:.2f}$"))
        counts = set(sel.get("carried_count", {}).values())
        carried = str(sorted(counts)[0]) if len(counts) == 1 else "varies"
        allowed = sel.get("selectable_counts", [])
        out.append(("Experiment 3", "Level count", f"{carried} levels on every slice",
                    "counts " + f"{min(allowed)} to {max(allowed)} selectable"
                    if allowed else "", "", f"${rq:.2f}$"))

    sc = load("exp4/scoping.csv")
    if sc is not None:
        out.append(("Experiment 4", "Prediction scope", "the whole session",
                    "the attended painting", "", f"${rc:.2f}$, ${rq:.2f}$"))

    lv = load("exp5/levers.csv")
    if lv is not None:
        out.append(("Experiment 5", "Personalisation", "none carried",
                    "baseline window, labelled warm-up, person-relative target",
                    "", f"${rc:.2f}$, ${rq:.2f}$"))
    return out


def main():
    body = []
    prev = None
    for exp, what, carried, against, span, margin in rows():
        if prev is not None:
            body.append("\\groupsep" if exp != prev else "\\rowsep")
        body.append(f"{exp} & {what} & {carried} & {against} & {span} & {margin} \\\\")
        prev = exp

    tex = r"""\chapter{Pipeline Configuration Summary}
\label{app:alt-supplementary}

Every choice the methodology makes, what was carried, what it was carried over, and the
margin the comparison was resolved at. A blank span means the candidates were not scored
against one another on a single number, either because the choice was fixed by a rule rather
than by a score or because the comparison is reported per slice in the chapter itself. A
selection made inside its margin is a convenience among candidates this cohort cannot
distinguish, not a claim that the carried one is better.

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\scriptsize
\caption{The carried pipeline, decision by decision, with the span between candidates and the margin each comparison was resolved at. Spans and margins are in the units of the score that decision was read on, \ac{CCC} for Experiments 1 and 2 and pooled \ac{QWK} for Experiments 3 to 5. A blank span means the candidates were not scored against one another on a single number, either because the choice was fixed by a rule rather than by a score or because the comparison is reported per slice in the results chapter; a blank margin means the entry states a measured margin rather than being resolved against one.}
\label{tab:alt-app-pipeline-summary}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}%
\setlength{\aboverulesep}{0pt}\setlength{\belowrulesep}{0pt}%
\begin{adjustbox}{max width=\linewidth, max totalheight=0.9\textheight}
\begin{tabular}{!{\tabedge}ll!{\colsepline}ll!{\colsepline}rr!{\tabedge}}
\toprule
Stage & Decision & Carried & Compared against & Span & Margin \\
\midrule
""" + "\n".join(body) + r"""
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{adjustbox}
\end{table}
"""
    open(TEX, "w").write(tex)
    print(f"written to {TEX}, {len(body)} lines")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/predictions.py.text:
"""Out-of-fold predictions of the standard model (CatBoost, nested-tuned as in
families.py) for every cell, saved per row: needed for pooled scores, calibration
checks, and Experiment 2's late fusion.
Usage: python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.predictions --stream rcea"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, json, pathlib, warnings
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from scripts.utils import RANDOM_SEED
from scripts.modeling.ccc_metrics import concordance_correlation_coefficient as ccc
from scripts.exp1_v2.features import get, OUT as FEAT_DIR
from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import usable_pids, SEL_DIR
from scripts.exp1_v2.families import fold_keys, assemble, SENSORS, AXES

OUT = pathlib.Path("results/exp1_v2/predictions"); OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def grid():
    from sklearn.ensemble import ExtraTreesRegressor
    return [ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_depth=d, random_state=RANDOM_SEED, n_jobs=4)
            for d in (None, 8, 4)]

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument("--stream", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    winners = json.loads((SEL_DIR / f"winners_{a.stream}.json").read_text())
    pids = [p for p in usable_pids(a.stream) if p in winners]
    for sensor in SENSORS:
        f = OUT / f"{a.stream}_{sensor}.parquet"
        if f.exists(): print(f"{sensor}: cached"); continue
        frames = []
        for axis in AXES:
            for o in pids:
                keys = fold_keys(winners, o, sensor, pids)
                X, ys, g = assemble(a.stream, pids, keys)
                y = ys[axis]
                ok = np.isfinite(y) & np.isfinite(X).any(axis=1)
                Xo, yo, go = X[ok], y[ok], g[ok]
                tr, te = go != o, go == o
                if te.sum() < 5 or tr.sum() < 50: continue
                gk = GroupKFold(min(5, len(np.unique(go[tr]))))
                def inner(m):
                    vals = []
                    for itr, ite in gk.split(Xo[tr], yo[tr], go[tr]):
                        pipe = Pipeline([("i", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                                         ("s", StandardScaler()), ("m", m)])
                        pipe.fit(Xo[tr][itr], yo[tr][itr])
                        vals.append(ccc(yo[tr][ite], pipe.predict(Xo[tr][ite])))
                    return float(np.nanmean(vals))
                best = max(grid(), key=inner)
                pipe = Pipeline([("i", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                                 ("s", StandardScaler()), ("m", best)])
                pipe.fit(Xo[tr], yo[tr])
                frames.append(pd.DataFrame({"fold": o, "axis": axis, "y": yo[te],
                                            "yhat": pipe.predict(Xo[te])}))
                print(f"{sensor}/{axis}/{o} done", flush=True)
        if frames:
            pd.concat(frames).to_parquet(f)
            print(f"-> {f}", flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/relations.py.text:
"""Sensor-annotation relations: within-participant Spearman correlation of every feature
against valence and arousal, tested across participants and false-discovery corrected.

Runs on either the default configuration (what each searched parameter carries before any
candidate is compared) or the configuration the sweep carried forward, so the two can be
compared rather than asserted equal.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.relations --config selected

Also writes the collinearity check behind the pupil near-misses: saccade frequency and the
window's sample count are the same quantity if the eye tracker's rate varies with the scene.
"""
import argparse
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import spearmanr, wilcoxon

from scripts.exp1_v2.features import DEFAULTS, OUT as FEAT_DIR

# The sweep carried the simplest candidate of each tied set (Results 4.2).
# Pupil and speech are unchanged from the default; only the EDA window and the
# HRV interbeat multiplier move.
SELECTED = {
    "pupil": "P_vt30_c0_t0",
    "eda": "E_nk_k5_w3",
    "hrv": "H_m3_t0",
    "speech_acoustics": "S_egemaps",
    "speech_content": "S_vader",
}

MIN_PAIRS = 30      # seconds a participant must contribute before their r is computed
MIN_PARTICIPANTS = 8  # at least half the smaller cohort
OUT = FEAT_DIR.parent


def load(keys):
    data = {}
    for stream in ("rcea", "retro"):
        frames = []
        for d in sorted(FEAT_DIR.glob(f"*_{stream}")):
            lab = pd.read_parquet(d / "labels.parquet")
            parts = [lab.rename(columns={"valence": "labels_valence",
                                         "arousal": "labels_arousal"})]
            for sensor, key in keys.items():
                f = d / f"{key}.parquet"
                if f.exists():
                    parts.append(pd.read_parquet(f).reindex(lab.index).add_prefix(f"{sensor}__"))
            df = pd.concat(parts, axis=1)
            df["participant"] = d.name.split("_")[0]
            frames.append(df)
        df = pd.concat(frames).rename(columns={"labels_valence": "valence",
                                               "labels_arousal": "arousal"})
        feats = [c for c in df.columns if "__" in c and df[c].notna().any()]
        data[stream] = (df, feats)
    return data


def relations(data):
    cells = []
    for stream, (df, feats) in data.items():
        for axis in ("valence", "arousal"):
            for feat in feats:
                rs = []
                for _, sub in df.groupby("participant"):
                    m = sub[feat].notna() & sub[axis].notna()
                    if m.sum() >= MIN_PAIRS:
                        r = spearmanr(sub.loc[m, feat], sub.loc[m, axis]).statistic
                        if np.isfinite(r):
                            rs.append(r)
                if len(rs) >= MIN_PARTICIPANTS:
                    cells.append(dict(stream=stream, axis=axis, feature=feat, n=len(rs),
                                      r_med=float(np.median(rs)),
                                      r_q1=float(np.quantile(rs, 0.25)),
                                      r_q3=float(np.quantile(rs, 0.75)),
                                      r_mean=float(np.mean(rs)),
                                      r_sd=float(np.std(rs, ddof=1)),
                                      r_min=float(np.min(rs)), r_max=float(np.max(rs)),
                                      _rs=rs))
    rel = pd.DataFrame(cells)
    rel["p"] = [wilcoxon(c["_rs"]).pvalue if any(r != 0 for r in c["_rs"]) else 1.0
                for c in cells]
    # Benjamini-Hochberg over every test at once
    pv = rel.p.values
    order = np.argsort(pv)
    ranked = pv[order] * len(pv) / (np.arange(len(pv)) + 1)
    q_sorted = np.minimum.accumulate(ranked[::-1])[::-1]
    q = np.empty_like(q_sorted)
    q[order] = np.clip(q_sorted, 0, 1)
    rel["q"] = q
    rel["sig"] = rel.q < 0.05
    return rel.drop(columns="_rs").sort_values(["stream", "axis", "feature"]).reset_index(drop=True)


def collinearity(data):
    """Within-participant correlation between saccade frequency, pupil diameter and the
    window's sample count. A high value means the eye-tracking 'signal' is recording density."""
    rows = []
    for stream, (df, _) in data.items():
        need = {"pupil__saccade_freq", "pupil__sample_count", "pupil__pupil_mean"}
        if not need <= set(df.columns):
            continue
        for pid, sub in df.groupby("participant"):
            s = sub[list(need)].dropna()
            if len(s) < MIN_PAIRS:
                continue
            rows.append(dict(
                stream=stream, participant=pid, n=len(s),
                saccade_vs_count=spearmanr(s["pupil__saccade_freq"],
                                           s["pupil__sample_count"]).statistic,
                diameter_vs_count=spearmanr(s["pupil__pupil_mean"],
                                            s["pupil__sample_count"]).statistic))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--config", choices=["default", "selected"], default="selected")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    keys = DEFAULTS if args.config == "default" else SELECTED
    print(f"{args.config} configuration: {keys}")
    data = load(keys)
    for stream, (df, feats) in data.items():
        print(f"  {stream}: {len(df):,} rows, {df.participant.nunique()} participants, "
              f"{len(feats)} features")

    rel = relations(data)
    path = OUT / f"relations_{args.config}.csv"
    rel.to_csv(path, index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(rel)} tests, {int(rel.sig.sum())} survive FDR at q<0.05 -> {path}")
    print(f"nominally significant before correction: {int((rel.p < 0.05).sum())} "
          f"({100 * (rel.p < 0.05).mean():.1f}%, chance expectation 5%)")
    print(rel.nsmallest(5, "q")[["stream", "axis", "feature", "n", "r_med", "p", "q"]]
          .to_string(index=False))

    col = collinearity(data)
    col.to_csv(OUT / f"relations_collinearity_{args.config}.csv", index=False)
    print("\ncollinearity with recording density (median within-participant Spearman):")
    print(col.groupby("stream")[["saccade_vs_count", "diameter_vs_count"]]
          .median().round(3).to_string())

    summary = dict(config=args.config, keys=keys, tests=int(len(rel)),
                   survivors=int(rel.sig.sum()),
                   nominal_p05=int((rel.p < 0.05).sum()),
                   max_abs_r_med=float(rel.r_med.abs().max()),
                   saccade_vs_count_median=float(col.saccade_vs_count.median()),
                   diameter_vs_count_median=float(col.diameter_vs_count.median()))
    (OUT / f"relations_{args.config}_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/relations_literature.py.text:
"""Compare each carried feature's observed relation to the direction the literature predicts.

Expectations are transcribed from sensor_affect_relations.md, which records a direction per
feature per axis with a confidence rating and citations. Only features that table names are
given an expectation: '+' and '-' are directional and testable by sign, '0' means no relation
is expected, and a feature the table does not commit on is carried as "no expectation" rather
than guessed. For the acoustic set, only the central-tendency parameter of each named family
is mapped, because the table commits on the quantity (pitch, loudness, jitter, shimmer, HNR)
and not on its spread or its slope.
"""
import pathlib

import pandas as pd
from scripts.exp1_v2.appendix_layout import fit_wide_tables
from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT

# (valence, arousal) as recorded in sensor_affect_relations.md, with its confidence rating.
EXPECTED = {
    # EDA
    "eda__eda_scr_count":           ("0", "+", "high",   "SCR frequency / count"),
    "eda__eda_scr_amp_mean":        ("0", "+", "high",   "SCR amplitude (mean)"),
    "eda__eda_scr_amp_median":      ("0", "+", "high",   "SCR amplitude (median)"),
    "eda__eda_scl_mean":            ("0", "+", "high",   "SCL (tonic level)"),
    # HRV
    "hrv__hrv_RMSSD":               ("0", "-", "high",   "RMSSD"),
    "hrv__hrv_HF":                  ("0", "-", "high",   "HF power"),
    "hrv__hrv_meanNN":              ("0", "-", "high",   "meanNN"),
    "hrv__hrv_SDNN":                ("0", "-", "medium", "SDNN"),
    # Pupil and gaze
    "pupil__pupil_mean":            ("0", "+", "high",   "Pupil dilation (mean)"),
    "pupil__fixation_duration":     ("?", "+", "medium", "Fixation duration"),
    "pupil__saccade_freq":          ("0", "*", "contested", "Saccade frequency"),
    "pupil__blink_rate":            ("?", "*", "low",    "Blink rate"),
    # Speech, acoustic: the central-tendency parameter of each named family only
    "speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_f0semitonefrom27_5hz_sma3nz_amean":
                                    ("?", "+", "medium", "Pitch (F0) mean"),
    "speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_loudness_sma3_amean":
                                    ("0", "+", "high",   "Energy / intensity"),
    "speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_jitterlocal_sma3nz_amean":
                                    ("0", "+", "medium", "Jitter"),
    "speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_shimmerlocaldb_sma3nz_amean":
                                    ("0", "+", "medium", "Shimmer"),
    "speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_hnrdbacf_sma3nz_amean":
                                    ("0", "-", "low",    "HNR"),
    # Speech, content
    "speech_content__vader_compound": ("+", "0", "high", "Sentiment score (VADER)"),
}
SOURCE = {'eda__eda_scr_count': 'Ayres 2021; Saganowski 2021; Sabour 2023', 'eda__eda_scr_amp_mean': 'Saganowski 2021; Ayres 2021', 'eda__eda_scr_amp_median': 'Saganowski 2021; Ayres 2021', 'eda__eda_scl_mean': 'Ayres 2021; Sabour 2023; Lorenzini 2023', 'hrv__hrv_RMSSD': 'Ishaque 2021; Arakaki 2023', 'hrv__hrv_HF': 'Ishaque 2021; Arakaki 2023', 'hrv__hrv_meanNN': 'Ishaque 2021; Tavakoli 2021', 'hrv__hrv_SDNN': 'Ishaque 2021; Arakaki 2023', 'pupil__pupil_mean': 'Mahanama 2022; Halbig 2021; Ayres 2021', 'pupil__fixation_duration': 'Mahanama 2022; Ayres 2021; Adhanom 2023', 'pupil__saccade_freq': 'Mahanama 2022; Adhanom 2023', 'pupil__blink_rate': 'Mahanama 2022; Halbig 2021', 'speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_f0semitonefrom27_5hz_sma3nz_amean': 'Wani 2021; Zhou 2023', 'speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_loudness_sma3_amean': 'Wani 2021; Zhou 2023', 'speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_jitterlocal_sma3nz_amean': 'Wani 2021; Menne 2024', 'speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_shimmerlocaldb_sma3nz_amean': 'Wani 2021; Menne 2024', 'speech_acoustics__speech_egemaps_hnrdbacf_sma3nz_amean': 'voice-quality literature, inferred', 'speech_content__vader_compound': 'Nandwani 2021; Menne 2024'}
NEAR_ZERO = 0.10  # |median rho| below which a '0' expectation is treated as met


def verdict(exp, rho):
    if exp in ("?", "*"):
        return "no expectation"
    if exp == "0":
        return "consistent" if abs(rho) < NEAR_ZERO else "larger than expected"
    return "agrees" if (rho > 0) == (exp == "+") else "opposite"


def main():
    rel = pd.read_csv(OUT / "relations_selected.csv")
    rows = []
    for feat, (ev, ea, conf, lit) in EXPECTED.items():
        for _, r in rel[rel.feature == feat].iterrows():
            exp = ev if r.axis == "valence" else ea
            rows.append(dict(stream=r.stream, axis=r.axis, feature=feat, literature=lit,
                             confidence=conf, expected=exp, r_med=round(r.r_med, 4),
                             n=int(r.n), q=round(r.q, 4), verdict=verdict(exp, r.r_med)))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["axis", "stream", "feature"])
    out.to_csv(OUT / "relations_literature.csv", index=False)

    d = out[out.expected.isin(["+", "-"])]
    print(f"features with a literature expectation: {out.feature.nunique()} of {rel.feature.nunique()} tested")
    print(f"directional tests (expected + or -): {len(d)}")
    print(f"  agrees   {(d.verdict == 'agrees').sum()}")
    print(f"  opposite {(d.verdict == 'opposite').sum()}")
    print(f"  surviving correction (q < 0.05): {(d.q < 0.05).sum()}")
    print()
    z = out[out.expected == "0"]
    print(f"'no relation expected' cells: {len(z)}, consistent {(z.verdict=='consistent').sum()}, "
          f"larger than expected {(z.verdict=='larger than expected').sum()}")
    print()
    print(d.to_string(index=False))
    print(f"\nwritten to {OUT / 'relations_literature.csv'}")




APPENDIX = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "research-proposal" / "appendix_final_exp1.tex"
START = "% BEGIN generated: literature-direction comparison\n"
END = "% END generated: literature-direction comparison\n"
NICE = {"eda": "\\ac{EDA}", "hrv": "\\ac{HRV}", "pupil": "Pupil",
        "speech_acoustics": "Speech ac.", "speech_content": "Speech con."}


def latex_table():
    d = pd.read_csv(OUT / "relations_literature.csv")
    order = ["pupil", "eda", "hrv", "speech_acoustics", "speech_content"]
    d = d[d.expected.isin(["+", "-"])].copy()
    d["sensor_key"] = d.feature.str.split("__").str[0]
    d["sensor_rank"] = d.sensor_key.map({s: i for i, s in enumerate(order)})
    d = d.sort_values(["sensor_rank", "literature", "stream"])
    rows, prev = [], None
    for i, (_, r) in enumerate(d.iterrows()):
        if i:
            rows.append("\\groupsep" if r.sensor_key != prev else "\\rowsep")
        prev = r.sensor_key
        sensor = NICE[r.sensor_key]
        rows.append(
            f"{sensor} & {r.literature} & {r.stream}, {r.axis} & ${r.expected}$ & "
            f"${r.r_med:+.4f}$ & {r.n} & ${r.q:.2f}$ & {r.verdict} & {SOURCE[r.feature]} \\\\")
    body = "\n".join(rows)
    return (START + r"""\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\scriptsize
\caption{Observed direction against the direction the literature predicts, for every carried
feature the modality literature commits a sign on, with the source as recorded when the expectations were compiled during the review. \emph{Expected} is
that sign; \emph{Median $r$} is the median within-participant Spearman correlation, so a
verdict of \emph{agrees} means the two share a sign. Features the literature does not commit on,
including the mel-frequency coefficients, carry no expectation and are absent, as are the
retrospective electrodermal cells, which fall below the eight visitors a coefficient requires.
No cell survives correction.}
\label{tab:alt-app-exp1-literature}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}%
\setlength{\aboverulesep}{0pt}\setlength{\belowrulesep}{0pt}%
\begin{tabular}{!{\tabedge}l!{\colsepline}l!{\colsepline}l!{\colsepline}c!{\colsepline}r!{\colsepline}r!{\colsepline}r!{\colsepline}l!{\colsepline}l!{\tabedge}}
\toprule
Sensor & Literature row & Slice & Expected & Median $r$ & $n$ & $q$ & Verdict & Source \\
\midrule
""" + body + r"""
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
""" + END)


def write_appendix():
    tex = APPENDIX.read_text()
    block = latex_table()
    if START in tex:
        a, b = tex.index(START), tex.index(END) + len(END)
        tex = tex[:a] + block + tex[b:]
    else:
        tex = tex.rstrip() + "\n\n" + block
    APPENDIX.write_text(fit_wide_tables(tex)[0])
    print(f"appendix table written to {APPENDIX.name}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
    write_appendix()

scripts/exp1_v2/resolution_qwk.py.text:
"""The selection resolution in quadratic-weighted-kappa units.

The resolution measured in selection.py is in CCC units, and Experiments 1 and 2 are
scored on CCC, so it governs their selections correctly. Experiments 3 to 5 are scored on
pooled QWK, which is a different scale with its own run-to-run variability, and a margin
measured on one cannot be assumed to hold for the other. This measures the second margin
by the identical procedure so that each metric's selections are resolved in their own
units.

Everything that can be held fixed is held fixed at what selection.py used: the same cell
(cardiac features against rcea arousal), the same starting configuration, the classifier
counterpart of the same random forest, the same twenty repeats, the same bootstrap
resampling of each fold's training participants, and the same p95 minus p5 statistic
rounded up to two decimal places.

Two things necessarily differ. The score is pooled once over every fold's held-out
predictions rather than averaged over folds, because that is how the ordinal experiments
report QWK. And QWK needs a level count: five is fixed here in advance, being the finest
of the coarse-end candidates and an odd count, so the scale midpoint falls inside a level
rather than on a boundary.

    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.resolution_qwk              # the pre-fixed margin
    python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.resolution_qwk --levels 3    # robustness only

Only the five-level run defines the margin. The other counts are a declared robustness
check on how much the margin depends on the count it was measured at, and they are
reported beside it rather than used to select anything.
"""
import argparse
import json

import numpy as np
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.metrics import cohen_kappa_score
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from scripts.exp1_v2.selection import OUT, load_matrix, usable_pids
from scripts.utils import RANDOM_SEED

STREAM, KEY, AXIS = "rcea", "H_m4_t0", "arousal"
LEVELS = 5
REPEATS = 20
OUT_FILE = OUT / "resolution_qwk.json"


def to_levels(y, levels=LEVELS):
    """Equal-width levels on the known 0 to 10 scale, edges fixed by design."""
    edges = np.linspace(0, 10, levels + 1)[1:-1]
    return np.digitize(np.clip(y, 0, 10), edges)


def one_repeat(r, X, y, g, pids):
    """One full leave-one-subject-out pass, with each fold's training participants
    resampled with replacement, returning the pooled QWK over every held-out row."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(RANDOM_SEED + r)
    true, pred = [], []
    for o in pids:
        tr_pids = [p for p in pids if p != o]
        boot = rng.choice(tr_pids, size=len(tr_pids), replace=True)
        tr, te = np.isin(g, boot), g == o
        if te.sum() < 5:
            continue
        pipe = Pipeline([("imp", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                         ("sc", StandardScaler()),
                         ("m", RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=300,
                                                      random_state=RANDOM_SEED + r,
                                                      n_jobs=1))])
        pipe.fit(X[tr], y[tr])
        true.append(y[te])
        pred.append(pipe.predict(X[te]))
    true, pred = np.concatenate(true), np.concatenate(pred)
    return float(cohen_kappa_score(true, pred, weights="quadratic",
                                   labels=list(range(LEVELS))))


def main():
    global LEVELS, OUT_FILE
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--levels", type=int, default=LEVELS)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.levels != LEVELS:
        LEVELS = args.levels
        OUT_FILE = OUT / f"resolution_qwk_b{LEVELS}.json"
    pids = usable_pids(STREAM)
    X, yv, ya, g = load_matrix(pids, STREAM, KEY)
    y = ya if AXIS == "arousal" else yv
    ok = np.isfinite(y) & np.isfinite(X).any(axis=1)
    X, y, g = X[ok], to_levels(y[ok], LEVELS), g[ok]
    print(f"{STREAM}/{KEY}/{AXIS}: {len(y):,} rows, {len(pids)} visitors, "
          f"{LEVELS} levels, level counts {np.bincount(y, minlength=LEVELS).tolist()}")

    means = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(delayed(one_repeat)(r, X, y, g, pids)
                                for r in range(REPEATS))
    lo, hi = np.percentile(means, [5, 95])
    res = float(np.ceil((hi - lo) * 100) / 100)
    OUT_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(
        {"repeat_pooled_qwk": means, "p5": lo, "p95": hi, "resolution_qwk": res,
         "cell": f"{STREAM}/{KEY}/{AXIS}", "levels": LEVELS, "repeats": REPEATS,
         "statistic": "pooled QWK over all held-out rows, one value per repeat"},
        indent=2))
    print(f"\nrepeat pooled QWK: min {min(means):+.4f}, max {max(means):+.4f}")
    print(f"resolution (QWK) = {res}  (p5 {lo:+.4f}, p95 {hi:+.4f}, {REPEATS} repeats)")
    print(f"written to {OUT_FILE}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

scripts/exp1_v2/selection.py.text:
"""
scripts/exp1_v2/selection.py
=============================
Configuration selection for Experiment 1 v2 (Methods 3.3.3) and the selection
resolution (Methods 3.1). See RUNBOOK.md.

The vote, per outer fold (held-out visitor o):
  candidates compete on the training participants alone. Every training
  participant q scores every candidate by inner-LOSO CCC (Ridge alpha=1 after
  median imputation + scaling; trained on training-minus-q), averaged over the
  two axes. Scores become ranks within q; best mean rank wins. Ties within the
  selection resolution on mean CCC resolve to the simpler candidate (candidate
  list order = declared simplicity order).

Sequential steps: pupil rule -> correction -> direction/delay (+ estimated);
HRV multiplier -> direction/delay (+ estimated); EDA decomposition x mask -> window.

Usage:
  python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.selection --resolution      # measure first
  python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.selection --stream rcea
  python3 -u -m scripts.exp1_v2.selection --stream retro
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from scripts.utils import RANDOM_SEED, RCEA_PARTICIPANTS, RETRO_PARTICIPANTS
from scripts.modeling.ccc_metrics import concordance_correlation_coefficient as ccc
from scripts.exp1_v2.features import get, analysed_index, OUT as FEAT_DIR

OUT = pathlib.Path("results/exp1_v2")
SEL_DIR = OUT / "selection"
SEL_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
RES_FILE = OUT / "resolution.json"

AXES = ("valence", "arousal")
DIRDELAYS = [f"{d}{k}" for d in ("t", "f") for k in range(7)]  # t0..t6, f0..f6


def usable_pids(stream: str) -> list[str]:
    pids = RCEA_PARTICIPANTS if stream == "rcea" else RETRO_PARTICIPANTS
    out = []
    for p in pids:
        lab = FEAT_DIR / f"{p}_{stream}" / "labels.parquet"
        if lab.exists() and len(pd.read_parquet(lab)):
            out.append(p)
    return out


def load_matrix(pids: list[str], stream: str, key: str):
    """Stacked (X, y_valence, y_arousal, groups) for one candidate key."""
    Xs, yv, ya, gs = [], [], [], []
    for p in pids:
        lab = pd.read_parquet(FEAT_DIR / f"{p}_{stream}" / "labels.parquet")
        f = get(p, stream, key, lab.index)
        f = f.reindex(lab.index)
        Xs.append(f.to_numpy(float))
        yv.append(lab["valence"].to_numpy(float))
        ya.append(lab["arousal"].to_numpy(float))
        gs.append(np.repeat(p, len(lab)))
    return (np.vstack(Xs), np.concatenate(yv), np.concatenate(ya), np.concatenate(gs))


def _ridge():
    return Pipeline([("imp", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                     ("sc", StandardScaler()), ("m", Ridge(alpha=1.0))])


def score_candidates(cands: list[str], train_pids: list[str], stream: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rows = training participants, columns = candidates; cell = inner-LOSO
    CCC (mean over axes). All candidates are scored on identical rows: rows
    with a label and at least one finite feature under EVERY candidate."""
    mats = {c: load_matrix(train_pids, stream, c) for c in cands}
    g = mats[cands[0]][3]
    ok = np.ones(len(g), bool)
    for X, yv, ya, _ in mats.values():
        ok &= np.isfinite(yv) & np.isfinite(ya) & np.isfinite(X).any(axis=1)

    def one_cell(c, q):
        X, yv, ya, gg = mats[c]
        tr = ok & (gg != q)
        te = ok & (gg == q)
        if te.sum() < 5 or tr.sum() < 50:
            return np.nan
        vals = []
        for y in (yv, ya):
            pipe = _ridge()
            pipe.fit(X[tr], y[tr])
            vals.append(ccc(y[te], pipe.predict(X[te])))
        return float(np.mean(vals))

    cells = Parallel(n_jobs=-1, prefer="threads")(delayed(one_cell)(c, q) for c in cands for q in train_pids)
    S = pd.DataFrame(np.array(cells, float).reshape(len(cands), len(train_pids)).T,
                     index=train_pids, columns=cands)
    return S


def vote(S: pd.DataFrame, resolution: float) -> dict:
    """Mean-rank winner with the tie resolved toward the simpler candidate
    (earlier column = simpler)."""
    ranks = S.rank(axis=1, ascending=False)
    mean_rank = ranks.mean()
    mean_ccc = S.mean()
    winner = mean_rank.idxmin()
    best_ccc = mean_ccc[winner]
    for c in S.columns:  # declared simplicity order
        if mean_ccc[best := c] >= best_ccc - resolution:
            winner_simple = c
            break
    return {"winner": winner_simple, "rank_winner": winner,
            "mean_rank": mean_rank.round(3).to_dict(),
            "mean_ccc": mean_ccc.round(4).to_dict()}


def dirdelay_step(prefix_fmt: str, train_pids: list[str], stream: str, resolution: float) -> dict:
    """Direction/delay sweep plus the estimated-vs-fixed comparison.
    prefix_fmt e.g. 'P_vt240_c0_{dd}' or 'H_m4_{dd}'."""
    cands = [prefix_fmt.format(dd=dd) for dd in DIRDELAYS]
    S = score_candidates(cands, train_pids, stream)
    fixed = vote(S, resolution)
    # per-participant estimated delay: each training participant's own best cell
    est_scores = S.max(axis=1)
    est_choice = S.idxmax(axis=1)
    S2 = S.copy()
    S2["__estimated__"] = est_scores
    est_vote = vote(S2[[fixed["winner"], "__estimated__"]], resolution)
    use_estimated = est_vote["winner"] == "__estimated__"
    dirs = est_choice.str.extract(r"_([tf])(\d)$")[0]
    dels = est_choice.str.extract(r"_([tf])(\d)$")[1].astype(float)
    maj_dir = dirs.mode().iloc[0] if len(dirs.mode()) else "t"
    med_delay = int(np.median(dels[dirs == maj_dir])) if (dirs == maj_dir).any() else 0
    return {"fixed": fixed, "estimated_wins": bool(use_estimated),
            "estimated_vote": {k: est_vote[k] for k in ("mean_rank", "mean_ccc")},
            "per_pid_estimate": est_choice.to_dict(),
            "heldout_dirdelay": f"{maj_dir}{med_delay}",
            "winner": ("__estimated__" if use_estimated else fixed["winner"])}


def select_fold(stream: str, train_pids: list[str], resolution: float) -> dict:
    out = {}
    # ---- pupil: rule -> correction -> direction/delay
    s1 = vote(score_candidates([f"P_{r}_c0_t0" for r in ("vt30", "vt240", "idt", "adaptive")],
                               train_pids, stream), resolution)
    rule = s1["winner"].split("_")[1]
    s2 = vote(score_candidates([f"P_{rule}_c0_t0", f"P_{rule}_c1_t0"], train_pids, stream), resolution)
    corr = s2["winner"].split("_")[2]
    s3 = dirdelay_step(f"P_{rule}_{corr}_{{dd}}", train_pids, stream, resolution)
    pupil_key = (f"P_{rule}_{corr}_{s3['heldout_dirdelay']}" if s3["estimated_wins"]
                 else s3["winner"])
    out["pupil"] = {"steps": [s1, s2, s3], "key": pupil_key}
    # ---- hrv: multiplier -> direction/delay
    h1 = vote(score_candidates([f"H_m{m}_t0" for m in (3, 4, 5)], train_pids, stream), resolution)
    mult = h1["winner"].split("_")[1]
    h2 = dirdelay_step(f"H_{mult}_{{dd}}", train_pids, stream, resolution)
    hrv_key = (f"H_{mult}_{h2['heldout_dirdelay']}" if h2["estimated_wins"] else h2["winner"])
    out["hrv"] = {"steps": [h1, h2], "key": hrv_key}
    # ---- eda: decomposition x mask (jointly, 12 s default) -> window
    joint = [f"E_{dec}_k{k}_w12" for dec in ("nk", "cvx") for k in (5, 3, 2)]
    e1 = vote(score_candidates(joint, train_pids, stream), resolution)
    dec, kk = e1["winner"].split("_")[1], e1["winner"].split("_")[2]
    e2 = vote(score_candidates([f"E_{dec}_{kk}_w{w}" for w in (3, 6, 8, 12, 20)],
                               train_pids, stream), resolution)
    out["eda"] = {"steps": [e1, e2], "key": e2["winner"]}
    out["speech_acoustics"] = {"key": "S_egemaps"}
    out["speech_content"] = {"key": "S_vader"}
    return out


def measure_resolution(repeats: int = 20) -> float:
    """Run-to-run variability of one configuration under resampled folds:
    default HRV rcea features, default random forest (seed = repeat), each
    fold's training participants bootstrap-resampled. Resolution = p95-p5 of
    the repeat means, rounded up to two decimals."""
    from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
    stream, key, axis = "rcea", "H_m4_t0", "arousal"
    pids = usable_pids(stream)
    X, yv, ya, g = load_matrix(pids, stream, key)
    y = ya if axis == "arousal" else yv
    ok = np.isfinite(y) & np.isfinite(X).any(axis=1)
    X, y, g = X[ok], y[ok], g[ok]

    def one_repeat(r):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(RANDOM_SEED + r)
        vals = []
        for o in pids:
            tr_pids = [p for p in pids if p != o]
            boot = rng.choice(tr_pids, size=len(tr_pids), replace=True)
            tr = np.isin(g, boot)
            te = g == o
            if te.sum() < 5:
                continue
            pipe = Pipeline([("imp", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                             ("sc", StandardScaler()),
                             ("m", RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=300, random_state=RANDOM_SEED + r,
                                                          n_jobs=1))])
            pipe.fit(X[tr], y[tr])
            vals.append(ccc(y[te], pipe.predict(X[te])))
        return float(np.mean(vals))

    means = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(delayed(one_repeat)(r) for r in range(repeats))
    lo, hi = np.percentile(means, [5, 95])
    res = float(np.ceil((hi - lo) * 100) / 100)
    RES_FILE.write_text(json.dumps({"repeat_means": means, "p5": lo, "p95": hi,
                                    "resolution": res, "cell": f"{stream}/{key}/{axis}",
                                    "repeats": repeats}, indent=2))
    print(f"resolution = {res}  (p5 {lo:+.4f}, p95 {hi:+.4f}, {repeats} repeats)")
    return res


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--stream", choices=("rcea", "retro"))
    ap.add_argument("--resolution", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--folds", nargs="*", default=None, help="subset of held-out pids (smoke)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.resolution:
        measure_resolution()
        return

    resolution = json.loads(RES_FILE.read_text())["resolution"]
    stream = args.stream
    pids = usable_pids(stream)
    folds = args.folds if args.folds else pids
    print(f"{stream}: {len(pids)} participants, resolution {resolution}", flush=True)
    results = {}
    outfile = SEL_DIR / f"winners_{stream}.json"
    if outfile.exists():
        results = json.loads(outfile.read_text())
    for o in folds:
        if o in results:
            print(f"fold {o}: cached", flush=True)
            continue
        train = [p for p in pids if p != o]
        results[o] = select_fold(stream, train, resolution)
        outfile.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1))
        keys = {s: results[o][s]["key"] for s in results[o]}
        print(f"fold {o}: {keys}", flush=True)
    print(f"-> {outfile}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
scripts/feature_engineering/experiments/deep_alignment.py
============================================================
Deep Canonical Correlation Analysis (DCCA, Andrew et al. 2013) and Deep
Canonical Time Warping (DCTW, Trigeorgis et al. 2016) -- the two alignment
methods Related Work discusses but the project had not implemented, added
per an explicit user request to test all windowing approaches, not only
argue them from prior work.

Both learn a pair of small MLP encoders, one per modality, whose outputs are
driven toward maximum canonical correlation. DCCA assumes the two views are
already synchronised at a common rate (this project's existing per-second
trailing-window features satisfy that); DCTW additionally alternates with a
dynamic-time-warping alignment step, so it can handle a lag between the two
signals without assuming they are already index-aligned.

Deliberately tiny networks (one hidden layer, heavy dropout) and fit fresh
inside each LOSO training fold only, matching this project's "no fitting on
the full dataset" rule and its small-N caution elsewhere (learned_rep_qwk.py,
deep_net_raw.py): with 15-37 people, anything bigger overfits before it
finishes training.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

DEVICE = "cpu"


class _Encoder(nn.Module):
    """One small MLP per view. LayerNorm + dropout are the only regularisers
    needed at this size; a single hidden layer avoids overfitting the tiny
    per-fold training set."""

    def __init__(self, in_dim: int, out_dim: int, hidden: int = 16, dropout: float = 0.3):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(in_dim, hidden), nn.LayerNorm(hidden), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden, out_dim),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x)


def cca_loss(h1: torch.Tensor, h2: torch.Tensor, out_dim: int, r1: float = 1e-3, r2: float = 1e-3,
             eps: float = 1e-9) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Negative sum of canonical correlations between h1 and h2 (Andrew et al. 2013,
    eq. 4-6): -trace((Sigma11^-1/2 Sigma12 Sigma22^-1/2)^T (...))^1/2, computed via
    eigendecomposition of the (regularised) view covariances. r1/r2 are the ridge
    terms that keep Sigma11/Sigma22 invertible with a small batch relative to the
    projection dimension -- required here since a LOSO training fold can be small."""
    n = h1.shape[0]
    h1 = h1 - h1.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
    h2 = h2 - h2.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)

    sigma12 = (h1.T @ h2) / (n - 1)
    sigma11 = (h1.T @ h1) / (n - 1) + r1 * torch.eye(h1.shape[1], device=h1.device)
    sigma22 = (h2.T @ h2) / (n - 1) + r2 * torch.eye(h2.shape[1], device=h2.device)

    def _inv_sqrt(m):
        # symmetric PSD matrix power via eigendecomposition, tiny eigenvalues floored
        # (same guard as coral_domain_alignment.py's _sym_power, same reasoning: a
        # near-singular covariance must not blow up the inverse-sqrt)
        vals, vecs = torch.linalg.eigh(m)
        vals = torch.clamp(vals, min=eps)
        return vecs @ torch.diag(vals.pow(-0.5)) @ vecs.T

    sigma11_inv_sqrt = _inv_sqrt(sigma11)
    sigma22_inv_sqrt = _inv_sqrt(sigma22)
    t_matrix = sigma11_inv_sqrt @ sigma12 @ sigma22_inv_sqrt
    # sum of the top out_dim singular values of T = correlation to maximise
    corr = torch.linalg.svdvals(t_matrix)[:out_dim].sum()
    return -corr


def fit_dcca(x1: np.ndarray, x2: np.ndarray, out_dim: int = 2, epochs: int = 200,
             lr: float = 1e-2, seed: int = 42) -> tuple[_Encoder, _Encoder, float, float]:
    """Fit a DCCA pair on paired, already-synchronised rows x1[i] <-> x2[i] (both
    [n, d]; both must be pre-imputed/finite). Returns (encoder1, encoder2, mu/sd
    stats folded into the encoders is NOT done here -- caller standardises).
    Returns (enc1, enc2, x1_mean/std handled by caller, final training -corr)."""
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    t1 = torch.tensor(x1, dtype=torch.float32)
    t2 = torch.tensor(x2, dtype=torch.float32)
    enc1 = _Encoder(x1.shape[1], out_dim)
    enc2 = _Encoder(x2.shape[1], out_dim)
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(list(enc1.parameters()) + list(enc2.parameters()), lr=lr, weight_decay=1e-4)
    enc1.train(); enc2.train()
    last_loss = float("nan")
    for _ in range(epochs):
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss = cca_loss(enc1(t1), enc2(t2), out_dim)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
        last_loss = float(loss.item())
    enc1.eval(); enc2.eval()
    return enc1, enc2, -last_loss  # training correlation achieved (positive = good)


def project(enc1: _Encoder, enc2: _Encoder, x1: np.ndarray, x2: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    with torch.no_grad():
        h1 = enc1(torch.tensor(x1, dtype=torch.float32)).numpy()
        h2 = enc2(torch.tensor(x2, dtype=torch.float32)).numpy()
    return h1, h2


def held_out_correlation(h1: np.ndarray, h2: np.ndarray, out_dim: int, eps: float = 1e-9) -> float:
    """Sum of the top `out_dim` canonical correlations between two ALREADY-PROJECTED
    views, computed on whatever rows are passed in -- pass held-out projections here,
    never the rows the encoders were trained on. This is the numpy/no-grad twin of
    cca_loss's own SVD-based measure, used only for evaluation (training correlation
    on the fit rows is not a trustworthy signal by itself: verify_deep_alignment.py's
    own case 2 found DCCA reports strong training-set "correlation" even between two
    independent random views, a standard finite-sample CCA overfitting artefact)."""
    n = h1.shape[0]
    h1 = h1 - h1.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    h2 = h2 - h2.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    sigma12 = (h1.T @ h2) / (n - 1)
    sigma11 = (h1.T @ h1) / (n - 1) + 1e-3 * np.eye(h1.shape[1])
    sigma22 = (h2.T @ h2) / (n - 1) + 1e-3 * np.eye(h2.shape[1])

    def _inv_sqrt(m):
        vals, vecs = np.linalg.eigh(m)
        vals = np.clip(vals, eps, None)
        return vecs @ np.diag(vals ** -0.5) @ vecs.T

    t_matrix = _inv_sqrt(sigma11) @ sigma12 @ _inv_sqrt(sigma22)
    svals = np.linalg.svd(t_matrix, compute_uv=False)
    return float(np.sum(svals[:out_dim]))


def _dtw_path(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Classic O(n*m) dynamic-time-warping alignment path between two projected
    sequences a [n,k] and b [m,k] (Euclidean local cost), used as DCTW's alignment
    half of the alternating optimisation (Trigeorgis et al. 2016, Algorithm 1)."""
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    cost = np.full((n + 1, m + 1), np.inf)
    cost[0, 0] = 0.0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            d = float(np.sum((a[i - 1] - b[j - 1]) ** 2))
            cost[i, j] = d + min(cost[i - 1, j], cost[i, j - 1], cost[i - 1, j - 1])
    path = []
    i, j = n, m
    while i > 0 and j > 0:
        path.append((i - 1, j - 1))
        choices = [cost[i - 1, j], cost[i, j - 1], cost[i - 1, j - 1]]
        step = int(np.argmin(choices))
        if step == 0:
            i -= 1
        elif step == 1:
            j -= 1
        else:
            i -= 1; j -= 1
    path.reverse()
    return path


def fit_dctw(seqs1: list[np.ndarray], seqs2: list[np.ndarray], out_dim: int = 2,
             outer_iters: int = 4, inner_epochs: int = 60, lr: float = 1e-2,
             seed: int = 42) -> tuple[_Encoder, _Encoder, float]:
    """Fit a DCTW pair on lists of per-participant sequences (variable length per
    participant, NOT required to be the same length or already aligned within a
    participant -- that is exactly what DTW resolves). Alternates: (1) project
    with the current encoders and find each participant's DTW path, (2) retrain
    the encoders on the resulting paired (aligned) rows, pooled across all
    participants in this fold. `seqs1[p]`/`seqs2[p]` are participant p's own
    [T_p, d] feature matrices, same modality-pair convention as fit_dcca."""
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    enc1 = _Encoder(seqs1[0].shape[1], out_dim)
    enc2 = _Encoder(seqs2[0].shape[1], out_dim)
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(list(enc1.parameters()) + list(enc2.parameters()), lr=lr, weight_decay=1e-4)
    last_corr = float("nan")

    for _ in range(outer_iters):
        # --- alignment half: DTW path per participant under the current projection ---
        enc1.eval(); enc2.eval()
        paired1, paired2 = [], []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for a_raw, b_raw in zip(seqs1, seqs2):
                a_h = enc1(torch.tensor(a_raw, dtype=torch.float32)).numpy()
                b_h = enc2(torch.tensor(b_raw, dtype=torch.float32)).numpy()
                path = _dtw_path(a_h, b_h)
                for i, j in path:
                    paired1.append(a_raw[i]); paired2.append(b_raw[j])
        p1 = np.stack(paired1); p2 = np.stack(paired2)
        t1 = torch.tensor(p1, dtype=torch.float32); t2 = torch.tensor(p2, dtype=torch.float32)

        # --- representation half: retrain encoders on the now-paired rows ---
        enc1.train(); enc2.train()
        for _ in range(inner_epochs):
            opt.zero_grad()
            loss = cca_loss(enc1(t1), enc2(t2), out_dim)
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()
            last_corr = -float(loss.item())
    enc1.eval(); enc2.eval()
    return enc1, enc2, last_corr

"""
scripts/feature_extraction/eda_features.py
============================================
Trailing 12s window EDA features, matching Bas's actual column schema:
  eda_motion_fraction, eda_scr_count, eda_scr_per_min, eda_scr_freq_hz,
  eda_scr_amp_mean, eda_scr_amp_median, eda_scr_amp_std,
  eda_scr_risetime_mean_s, eda_scr_risetime_median_s,
  eda_scl_mean, eda_scl_std, eda_scl_slope_per_sample
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EDA_WINDOW_S = 12

_COLS = ["eda_motion_fraction", "eda_scr_count", "eda_scr_per_min", "eda_scr_freq_hz",
         "eda_scr_amp_mean", "eda_scr_amp_median", "eda_scr_amp_std",
         "eda_scr_risetime_mean_s", "eda_scr_risetime_median_s",
         "eda_scl_mean", "eda_scl_std", "eda_scl_slope_per_sample"]


def extract_eda_features_at_t(eda_df: pd.DataFrame, t: pd.Timestamp,
                               window_s: int = EDA_WINDOW_S, direction: str = "trailing") -> dict:
    # "trailing" = [t-w, t] (signal up to the annotation); "forward" = [t, t+w] (the post-annotation
    # response, matching van der Kaaden's "T_annotation + w" description). See window-direction diagnostic.
    lo, hi = (t, t + pd.Timedelta(seconds=window_s)) if direction == "forward" \
        else (t - pd.Timedelta(seconds=window_s), t)
    window = eda_df.loc[lo:hi]
    result = {c: np.nan for c in _COLS}
    if window.empty or len(window) < 2:
        return result

    if "motion_flag" in window.columns:
        result["eda_motion_fraction"] = float(window["motion_flag"].mean())

    if "scr_peaks" in window.columns and "eda_phasic" in window.columns:
        peak_mask = window["scr_peaks"] == 1
        n_peaks = int(peak_mask.sum())
        result["eda_scr_count"] = n_peaks
        result["eda_scr_per_min"] = n_peaks / (window_s / 60.0)
        result["eda_scr_freq_hz"] = n_peaks / window_s

        if n_peaks > 0:
            peak_amps = window.loc[peak_mask, "eda_phasic"].values
            result["eda_scr_amp_mean"] = float(np.nanmean(peak_amps))
            result["eda_scr_amp_median"] = float(np.nanmedian(peak_amps))
            result["eda_scr_amp_std"] = float(np.nanstd(peak_amps)) if len(peak_amps) > 1 else 0.0

            dt_s = (window.index[1] - window.index[0]).total_seconds() if len(window) > 1 else 0.25
            phasic = window["eda_phasic"].values
            peak_idx = np.where(peak_mask.values)[0]
            rise_times_s = []
            for pi in peak_idx:
                look_back = max(0, pi - int(5 / max(dt_s, 1e-6)))
                segment = phasic[look_back:pi]
                if len(segment) > 0:
                    trough_offset = np.argmin(segment)
                    rise_times_s.append((pi - (look_back + trough_offset)) * dt_s)
            if rise_times_s:
                result["eda_scr_risetime_mean_s"] = float(np.mean(rise_times_s))
                result["eda_scr_risetime_median_s"] = float(np.median(rise_times_s))
        else:
            result["eda_scr_amp_mean"] = result["eda_scr_amp_median"] = result["eda_scr_amp_std"] = 0.0

    if "eda_tonic" in window.columns:
        tonic = window["eda_tonic"].dropna().values
        if len(tonic) >= 2:
            result["eda_scl_mean"] = float(np.mean(tonic))
            result["eda_scl_std"] = float(np.std(tonic))
            result["eda_scl_slope_per_sample"] = float(np.polyfit(np.arange(len(tonic)), tonic, 1)[0])

    return result


def extract_eda_features_aligned(eda_df: pd.DataFrame, annotation_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
                                  window_s: int = EDA_WINDOW_S, direction: str = "trailing") -> pd.DataFrame:
    rows = [extract_eda_features_at_t(eda_df, t, window_s, direction) for t in annotation_index]
    feat = pd.DataFrame(rows, index=annotation_index)
    feat.index.name = "utc"
    return feat


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from scripts.annotation.rcea_alignment import load_rcea_aligned
    from scripts.preprocessing.eda_processing import process_eda
    from scripts.utils import RCEA_PARTICIPANTS

    pid = RCEA_PARTICIPANTS[0]
    proc = process_eda(pid)
    annot = load_rcea_aligned(pid)
    feat = extract_eda_features_aligned(proc, annot.index)
    print(feat.describe())
    print("missing:", feat.isna().mean().round(3).to_dict())

"""
scripts/feature_extraction/hrv_features.py
============================================
Trailing 60s window HRV features, matching Bas's actual column schema:
  hrv_n_intervals, hrv_meanNN_ms, hrv_SDNN_ms, hrv_RMSSD_ms, hrv_pNN50_pct,
  hrv_VLF, hrv_LF, hrv_HF, hrv_LFHF, hrv_SD1, hrv_SD2, hrv_SD1SD2

Frequency-domain: Welch PSD on the interpolated NN tachogram (van der Kaaden's
detailed-methods description, "Welch's method" on the interpolated tachogram),
integrating power over VLF/LF/HF. This replaces an earlier neurokit2.hrv_frequency()
wrapper that (a) returned VLF as all-NaN at a 60 s window and (b) produced LF/HF on an
absolute scale 20-165x his released values. The tachogram-Welch here populates VLF (as
his shipped data does, ~93% non-missing) and matches his absolute power scale. NOTE: at
a 60 s window VLF and the low edge of LF are under-resolved (VLF's 0.0033 Hz needs ~5 min);
they are emitted to match his schema but are not physiologically reliable at this length.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HRV_WINDOW_S = 60
HRV_INTERP_RATE = 4.0  # Hz; uniform grid the NN tachogram is resampled onto before the Welch PSD

_COLS = ["hrv_n_intervals", "hrv_meanNN_ms", "hrv_SDNN_ms", "hrv_RMSSD_ms", "hrv_pNN50_pct",
         "hrv_VLF", "hrv_LF", "hrv_HF", "hrv_LFHF", "hrv_SD1", "hrv_SD2", "hrv_SD1SD2"]


def _time_domain(nn_ms: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    diff_nn = np.diff(nn_ms)
    return {
        "hrv_n_intervals": len(nn_ms),
        "hrv_meanNN_ms": float(np.mean(nn_ms)),
        "hrv_SDNN_ms": float(np.std(nn_ms, ddof=1)) if len(nn_ms) > 1 else np.nan,
        "hrv_RMSSD_ms": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(diff_nn ** 2))) if len(diff_nn) else np.nan,
        "hrv_pNN50_pct": float(np.mean(np.abs(diff_nn) > 50) * 100) if len(diff_nn) else np.nan,
    }


def _frequency_domain(nn_window: pd.Series, interp_rate: float = HRV_INTERP_RATE) -> dict:
    """Welch PSD on the interpolated NN tachogram (van der Kaaden's method).

    nn_window is a UTC-indexed cleaned NN-interval series (ms) inside the window. It is placed on
    its beat-time axis, resampled to a uniform `interp_rate` grid, mean-removed (so band power is
    variability, not the mean level), and a Welch periodogram is integrated over the standard bands
    VLF [0.0033, 0.04], LF [0.04, 0.15], HF [0.15, 0.4] Hz. Power is in ms^2, matching his released
    absolute scale. Returns NaN for any band with too few resolvable bins at this window length.
    """
    from scipy import signal as sps

    nan_result = {"hrv_VLF": np.nan, "hrv_LF": np.nan, "hrv_HF": np.nan, "hrv_LFHF": np.nan}
    nn = nn_window.dropna()
    if len(nn) < 8:
        return nan_result

    t_s = (nn.index - nn.index[0]).total_seconds().to_numpy(dtype=float)
    vals = nn.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    dur = float(t_s[-1])
    n = int(round(dur * interp_rate))
    if dur <= 0 or n < 16:
        return nan_result

    grid = np.linspace(0.0, dur, n)
    tach = np.interp(grid, t_s, vals)
    tach = tach - tach.mean()
    try:
        freqs, psd = sps.welch(tach, fs=interp_rate, nperseg=min(len(tach), 256))
    except Exception:
        # Degenerate spectra (constant window etc.) are correctly returned as NaN; a *systematic*
        # failure shows up as ~100% NaN in the Phase 1.9 comparison table, the intended detector.
        return nan_result

    df = float(freqs[1] - freqs[0]) if len(freqs) > 1 else np.nan  # uniform bin width

    def _band(lo, hi):
        # Rectangular band power (sum of PSD bins x bin width). Standard, and unlike a trapezoid it
        # still returns a value when a band spans only one resolvable bin -- which VLF does at a 60 s
        # window (this is why Bas's shipped VLF is populated where a stricter rule would null it).
        m = (freqs >= lo) & (freqs < hi)
        return float(psd[m].sum() * df) if (int(m.sum()) >= 1 and np.isfinite(df)) else np.nan

    vlf, lf, hf = _band(0.0033, 0.04), _band(0.04, 0.15), _band(0.15, 0.4)
    lfhf = lf / hf if (hf is not None and np.isfinite(hf) and hf > 0) else np.nan
    return {"hrv_VLF": vlf, "hrv_LF": lf, "hrv_HF": hf, "hrv_LFHF": lfhf}


def _nonlinear(nn_ms: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    nan_result = {"hrv_SD1": np.nan, "hrv_SD2": np.nan, "hrv_SD1SD2": np.nan}
    if len(nn_ms) < 3:
        return nan_result
    diff_nn = np.diff(nn_ms)
    sd1 = float(np.std(diff_nn, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(2))
    # Canonical Poincare SD2 (Brennan 2001, as used by NeuroKit): SD2^2 = 2*Var(NN) - 0.5*Var(dNN).
    # The factor of 2 on Var(NN) was previously missing, which halved SD2 and inverted SD1/SD2
    # (ours ~2.05 vs Bas's physiologically-normal ~0.82); restoring it matches his released values.
    sd2 = float(np.sqrt(max(2 * np.var(nn_ms, ddof=1) - 0.5 * np.var(diff_nn, ddof=1), 0)))
    return {"hrv_SD1": sd1, "hrv_SD2": sd2, "hrv_SD1SD2": sd1 / sd2 if sd2 > 0 else np.nan}


def extract_hrv_features_at_t(nn_series: pd.Series, t: pd.Timestamp,
                               window_s: int = HRV_WINDOW_S, direction: str = "trailing",
                               interp_rate: float = HRV_INTERP_RATE) -> dict:
    # "trailing" = [t-w, t]; "forward" = [t, t+w] (post-annotation response, matching Bas's
    # "T_annotation + w" description). Time/nonlinear/frequency features all read the same window.
    lo, hi = (t, t + pd.Timedelta(seconds=window_s)) if direction == "forward" \
        else (t - pd.Timedelta(seconds=window_s), t)
    nn_window = nn_series.loc[lo:hi].dropna()
    if len(nn_window) < 2:
        return {c: np.nan for c in _COLS}

    window_nn = nn_window.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    feat = {}
    feat.update(_time_domain(window_nn))
    feat.update(_frequency_domain(nn_window, interp_rate))
    feat.update(_nonlinear(window_nn))
    return feat


def extract_hrv_features_aligned(nn_series: pd.Series, annotation_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
                                  window_s: int = HRV_WINDOW_S, direction: str = "trailing") -> pd.DataFrame:
    rows = [extract_hrv_features_at_t(nn_series, t, window_s, direction) for t in annotation_index]
    feat = pd.DataFrame(rows, index=annotation_index)
    feat.index.name = "utc"
    return feat


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from scripts.annotation.rcea_alignment import load_rcea_aligned
    from scripts.preprocessing.hrv_processing import process_hrv
    from scripts.utils import RCEA_PARTICIPANTS

    pid = RCEA_PARTICIPANTS[0]
    nn, _, _, _removed = process_hrv(pid)
    annot = load_rcea_aligned(pid)
    feat = extract_hrv_features_aligned(nn, annot.index)
    print(feat.describe())
    print("missing:", feat.isna().mean().round(3).to_dict())

"""
scripts/feature_extraction/text_features.py
=============================================
Phase 3 (rank 6): speech TEXT / sentiment features — the one principled shot at
the stubborn VALENCE axis. Lexical content is the literature's single best-supported
speech->valence signal, and it was entirely absent from the pipeline until now
(the schema was matched to Bas's aligned CSV, which omitted it).

Primary feature (always available): `text_vader_compound` — VADER compound sentiment
of each utterance's text, in [-1, +1], a direct valence proxy.

Optional (only if an NRC-VAD lexicon file is provided): `text_nrc_valence`,
`text_nrc_arousal`, `text_nrc_dominance` — mean over the utterance's content tokens.
The lexicon is NOT bundled (gated behind a form / not downloadable here); pass its
path to enable these columns, otherwise they're simply absent.

Alignment: sentiment is computed per transcript SEGMENT (utterance) and assigned to
the 1 Hz annotation seconds spanned by that segment's word activity — i.e. only where
speech is actually present; every other second is NaN (no text). This uses the
transcripts' true UTC timeline (dt_start/dt_end), which is unaffected by the acoustic
frame-alignment bug fixed elsewhere.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

_VADER_COL = "vader_compound"
_NRC_COLS = ["nrc_valence", "nrc_arousal", "nrc_dominance"]
_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z']+")


def _vader_analyzer():
    from vaderSentiment.vaderSentiment import SentimentIntensityAnalyzer
    return SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()


def load_nrc_vad(path: str | pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """Load an NRC-VAD lexicon (tab-separated: word, valence, arousal, dominance).
    Returns {} if the file is absent so callers degrade to VADER-only."""
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    if not path.exists():
        return {}
    lex = {}
    df = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", header=None, names=["word", "v", "a", "d"])
    for w, v, a, d in df.itertuples(index=False):
        lex[str(w).lower()] = (float(v), float(a), float(d))
    return lex


def _nrc_means(text: str, lex: dict) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    toks = [t for t in _TOKEN_RE.findall(str(text).lower()) if t in lex]
    if not toks:
        return np.nan, np.nan, np.nan
    arr = np.array([lex[t] for t in toks], dtype=float)
    return float(arr[:, 0].mean()), float(arr[:, 1].mean()), float(arr[:, 2].mean())


def extract_text_features_aligned(
    segments: pd.DataFrame,
    annotation_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
    nrc_lexicon_path: str | pathlib.Path | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Per-utterance sentiment aligned to the 1 Hz annotation timeline. `segments` must
    have `text`, `dt_start`, `dt_end` (from load_transcript_segments). Seconds with no
    overlapping speech are NaN.
    """
    lex = load_nrc_vad(nrc_lexicon_path) if nrc_lexicon_path else {}
    cols = [_VADER_COL] + (_NRC_COLS if lex else [])
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=annotation_index, columns=cols)
    if segments.empty:
        out.index.name = "utc"
        return out

    analyzer = _vader_analyzer()
    # precompute per-segment scores once (cheap; a handful of utterances per session)
    seg_scores = []
    for seg in segments.itertuples(index=False):
        text = getattr(seg, "text", "") or ""
        compound = analyzer.polarity_scores(text)["compound"] if text.strip() else np.nan
        row = {_VADER_COL: compound}
        if lex:
            v, a, d = _nrc_means(text, lex)
            row.update({"nrc_valence": v, "nrc_arousal": a, "nrc_dominance": d})
        seg_scores.append((seg.dt_start, seg.dt_end, row))

    # assign each annotation second to the segment whose [dt_start, dt_end] contains it
    for t in annotation_index:
        for dt_start, dt_end, row in seg_scores:
            if dt_start <= t <= dt_end:
                for c in cols:
                    out.at[t, c] = row.get(c, np.nan)
                break
    out.index.name = "utc"
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from scripts.annotation.rcea_alignment import load_rcea_aligned
    from scripts.preprocessing.speech_processing import load_transcript_segments
    from scripts.utils import RCEA_PARTICIPANTS

    pid = RCEA_PARTICIPANTS[0]
    seg = load_transcript_segments(pid)
    annot = load_rcea_aligned(pid)
    feat = extract_text_features_aligned(seg, annot.index)
    print(f"{pid}: shape={feat.shape}, cols={list(feat.columns)}")
    print(f"  vader_compound non-null={feat['vader_compound'].notna().mean():.3f} "
          f"(= fraction of seconds with speech); mean when present={feat['vader_compound'].mean():.3f}")
